# /sc:workflow protocol

Invoked only via `/sc:workflow` Activation. Plan only. Wave 2 is **Synthesize**.

## Execution vocabulary

| Verb | Tool |
|------|------|
| Load ref | Read |
| Write artifact | Write |
| Invoke Skill | Skill (`sc:reflect-protocol` in Wave 4; `sc:implement-protocol` only on `--handoff implement`) |
| Codegraph lookup | `mcp__codegraph__codegraph_<tool>` (exact names), only when `index_state` is `fresh` |

## Codegraph grounding

Rules, the closed `graph:*` token list and the caller-row, cap and read-before-cite rules are in `~/.claude/CODEGRAPH.md` (section 2 readiness, section 3 tokens, sections 5 and 6 rules, caps and `shown/total`). This protocol points there and copies none of it.

- **One readiness check per run.** Step 0 of Wave 1 (the package exists, before any lookup) runs section 2 of the guide once. It records `index_state`, `checked_at`, `worktree_root`, `projectPath`, the access mode and any `graph:*` token under `## Run state` in `<pkg>/artifacts/codegraph-grounding.md`. Later waves read that record and never run the check again.
- **Fresh only.** Codegraph runs only when `index_state` is `fresh` and its lookup tools are listed, with `projectPath` on every call. In any other state, or when a lookup fails or returns nothing, that step uses Grep, Glob and Read (the permanent floor, normal evidence) and the matching `graph:*` token goes into the grounding note. This never stops the run, fails the gate or changes the package status.
- **Rows are leads.** A graph row locates code and is not a citation: Read the range before a task names it. A caller row gives the caller's definition, so a task says "calls X" only after the call site is confirmed under guide section 5; otherwise it names the caller as a dependent. An empty answer never means "no callers".

| Step | Job | Codegraph tool when fresh | Floor |
|------|-----|---------------------------|-------|
| Wave 1, step 0 | Readiness check | `codegraph_status {projectPath}` | guarded CLI `status` per the guide, else the floor |
| Wave 1 | Resolve the files and symbols the source names; outline each named file | `codegraph_search {query, kind?, limit}`, `codegraph_node {file, symbolsOnly:true}`, and for an area overview `codegraph_files {format:"grouped", maxDepth:2}` (outside `allowed-tools`: called only when the session lists it, else Glob) | Glob, Grep for definitions, Read |
| Wave 2 | Body of each changed symbol; real callers and dependents; blast radius | `codegraph_node {symbol, file?, includeCode:true}`, `codegraph_callers {symbol, file?, limit}`, `codegraph_callees`, `codegraph_impact {symbol, depth:1}` | Grep with a word-boundary pattern, then Read each site |
| Wave 4 pre-check | The same lookups, read-only | the same tools | the same floor |

- **Sub-agent briefs.** Any brief this protocol writes for a sub-agent carries `index_state`, `checked_at`, `worktree_root` and the `projectPath` to pass; the receiver calls codegraph only when `index_state: fresh`, otherwise Grep and Read. The Wave 4 `/sc:reflect --mode pre` call takes flags only, so it cannot receive that state: reflect runs its own readiness check, which this run does not count as a second one.
- **Artifact.** `<pkg>/artifacts/codegraph-grounding.md` has the sections `## Run state`, `## Resolved symbols`, `## Dependents` and `## Pre-check`. It is a file this run wrote, so under `--unattended` it is listed in `artifacts` by the rule "every other file the run wrote" in the `## Unattended mode` section of the `workflow` command file. It adds no plan field and no contract key.

## Wave 0 — Parse

**Ref:** `refs/input-parse.md`

Entry: `"Add owner-approved format forgiveness to the Sweep Sheet ledger parser, reported strict and lenient per arm." --depth standard --handoff none`. Validate all input and flags first (`--output` is retired → `E-LEGACY`); only then create the exclusive package `.dev/tasks/to-do/<id>/` and write the `source.md` snapshot (every source, file or prompt). Exit: source snapshot, flags, package `<pkg>`.

STOP codes in the ref. No package, no plan file, no yaml on a pre-creation STOP.

`.dev/tasks/` is always staged (`git add .dev/tasks`): the package and its `artifacts/` included. Never gitignore it, never leave it untracked, and never write "never stage" about it in a generated plan (Constraints included). Staging is not committing.

Under `--unattended` that staging is deferred to the coordinator (`~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`): this run does not stage `.dev/tasks`. Also apply the `## Unattended mode` section of the `workflow` command file: the installed copy `~/.claude/commands/sc/workflow.md`, or the project copy `.claude/commands/sc/workflow.md`.

`--strategy enterprise` and omitted `--depth` → set `deep` + INFO.

## Wave 1 — Structure

**Ref:** `refs/phase-templates.md`

Entry: readable source. Exit: phase list with Goal/Inputs/Outputs/Checkpoint/deps.

Step 0 (once per run): the codegraph readiness check of `## Codegraph grounding`; then resolve the files and symbols the source names (codegraph when fresh, else Glob, Grep and Read) and record them under `## Resolved symbols` in `<pkg>/artifacts/codegraph-grounding.md`.

If nothing actionable → STOP `E-NO-PHASES`.

Depth caps phase count (quick 2–4, standard 4–8, deep 6–12).

## Wave 2 — Synthesize

Write `<pkg>/<id>.md` (the full package directory basename + `.md`, e.g. `TASK-WF-authLogin-20261001-063000.md`; never `plan.md`) from the bundled `refs/00_mdtm_template_simple_task.md`: Read it from this skill's directory and follow the rules in its HTML comment, then remove the comment and unused placeholders. Frontmatter keys (schema `workflow-plan/1.2`, `slug` = package id, `source: ./source.md`) and fill rules: `refs/quality-gates.md`.

Each Wave 1 phase → `## Phase N:` then its `## Task N:` headings (numbered 1..N across the plan). Phase Inputs → files/sections named in the task body; Outputs → the body and `Acceptance criteria:` of the task that produces each one (every Output lands in some task); Checkpoint → the last task's `Acceptance criteria:`; deps → `Depends on: Task K`.

Ground each task in the real code: its body names the real files and symbols it changes (repo-relative), and its `Acceptance criteria:` name the real callers and dependents that must keep working or be updated (recorded under `## Dependents` of the grounding artifact; codegraph when fresh, else Grep and Read). Size and order tasks by blast radius: a symbol with many dependents gets its own task, the tasks that update its dependents follow it with `Depends on: Task K`, and a change reaching more files than one task can hold is split, still within the depth cap.

`source.md` MUST already exist from Wave 0 (snapshot of the file or the inline prompt) before `<id>.md` is written.

## Wave 3 — Gate

**Ref:** `refs/quality-gates.md`

quick = schema-min. standard/deep = full. Fail → STOP `E-GATE`.

## Wave 4 — Reflect

**Pre-check (advisory, before the reflect call).** For each task, confirm that the files it names exist, its symbols resolve and its listed dependents are real, and list dependents of the touched symbols that no task names (codegraph when fresh, else Grep, Glob and Read; no new readiness check). Write the result under `## Pre-check` in `<pkg>/artifacts/codegraph-grounding.md` and print a one-line count with the plan path. It never edits `<id>.md` and never changes `status`; a failure of this step is only a `graph:*` note.

Final step of plan generation; runs only after Wave 3 passed, and **before** the Wave 5 contract and any `--handoff` (so an unreflected plan is never implemented). Invoke `/sc:reflect --mode pre --spec <pkg>/source.md --tasklist <pkg>/<id>.md` via Skill (`sc:reflect-protocol`), defaults for every other flag, no `--remediate`. Record reflect's `status` and `report_path` (from its `return-contract.yaml`) as `reflect_status` / `reflect_report_path`, and print both with the plan path.

Under `--unattended` (shared rules: `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`) that call passes `--unattended --output <report-dir>/nested/reflect-<n>/` (reflect's own directory flag; workflow's `--output` stays retired; `<n>` counts from 1 and is never reused), still without `--remediate`, and the nested contract is listed in `artifacts`, also when the call failed.

Advisory and read-only: never edit, delete, or regenerate `<id>.md` from findings, and never change the workflow `status` because of them. Reflect unavailable or `failed` → `reflect_status: skipped|failed`, `reflect_report_path: null`, one `unresolved` line; still proceed to Wave 5.

## Wave 5 — Contract

**Refs:** `refs/return-contract.md`, `refs/overlap-routing.md`

Write `<pkg>/return-contract.yaml` (contract 1.1: stable `slug`, `./<id>.md`, `./source.md`, `reflect_*`) **before** any `implement` handoff. Apply handoff; a failed `implement` handoff on a valid plan is `partial`, a failed generation is `failed`.

After an `implement` handoff the package may have moved to `done/` (executor-owned archive). Resolve the actual location by id (`.dev/tasks/to-do/<id>` vs `.dev/tasks/done/<id>`, `test -e || test -L`): only if the package still exists at `to-do/` may you rewrite the contract (e.g. to `partial`), and never recreate a directory or write into a path whose package is absent. Only `done/` exists → leave the archived contract untouched, report the failure/outcome in chat, print the actual `done/` plan path. Both exist → mutate neither and report the conflict. Print the plan path at its actual location.

## Will / Will Not

**Will:** one new package `.dev/tasks/to-do/<id>/` with `<id>.md`, `source.md`, `return-contract.yaml`; ground the plan in the real code through codegraph when the index is fresh. Never overwrites or reuses an existing package. Run `/sc:reflect --mode pre` (advisory) on the gated plan as the final generation step, before any handoff.

**Will Not:** product code, tasklist files, roadmap CLI, new agents, Task fan-out; modify the plan from reflect findings.

```yaml
schema: workflow-plan/1.2
source: ./source.md
strategy: systematic|agile|enterprise
depth: quick|standard|deep
slug: <id>
version: "1"
priority: High|Medium|Low
created_date: "YYYY-MM-DD"
```

Field rules (outside the machine example; write values bare, never with trailing `#` comments): `source` is the package-relative snapshot, never the original absolute path. `slug` equals the package directory name, e.g. `TASK-WF-authLogin-20261001-063000`. `priority` is the source's own priority, else `Medium`; never inferred. `created_date` is today (UTC) from the session date; never invented.

Body = `00_mdtm_template_simple_task.md` shape: `# <title>`, `Source: ./source.md`, `Goal:`, optional `## Constraints`, `## Phase N:` group headings, `## Task N:` items with `Acceptance criteria:`.

Operational lookup fields and links are package-relative (`./…`) or repo-relative; none may embed an absolute path or an old `.dev/tasks/to-do/` prefix (the package later moves to `done/`). Quoting source text or forensic paths in prose is fine.

Fail any check → STOP `E-GATE`. A plan that fails the gate is deleted (the draft this run wrote, nothing else) and the package keeps `source.md` plus a `failed` contract; a failed package is never executable. Do not leave a partial `<id>.md` claimed as success.

1	# Return contract 1.1
2	
3	Write `.dev/tasks/to-do/<id>/return-contract.yaml`. Paths inside the package are package-relative (`./…`) so the file stays valid after the package moves to `done/`:
4	
5	```yaml
6	contract_version: "1.1"
7	status: success | partial | failed
8	slug: <id>
9	plan_path: ./<id>.md | null
10	source_path: ./source.md | null
11	source_origin: <original path or "inline">   # informational only; never used for lookup
12	strategy: systematic | agile | enterprise
13	depth: quick | standard | deep
14	handoff_action: none | design | implement | tasklist
15	handoff_output_path: ./progress.md | null
16	reflect_status: success | partial | failed | skipped   # Wave 4 `/sc:reflect --mode pre`; advisory only
17	reflect_report_path: <abs path to reflect REPORT.md> | null
18	unresolved: []
19	```
20	
21	`reflect_*` are additive and advisory: they never change `status`. A generation `failed` contract (reflect never ran) uses `reflect_status: skipped`, `reflect_report_path: null`.
22	
23	## Status
24	
25	| Situation | status | plan_path |
26	|-----------|--------|-----------|
27	| Plan gated; handoff `none`/`design`/`tasklist` text emitted, or `implement` accepted | `success` | `./<id>.md` |
28	| Plan gated but the `--handoff implement` invocation failed (skill missing, implement STOP) | `partial` | `./<id>.md` — the plan stays valid and executable; list the reason in `unresolved` |
29	| Package exists but generation failed (`E-NO-PHASES`, `E-GATE`, write error) | `failed` | `null` (`source_path` `./source.md` if the snapshot was written, else `null`) |
30	
31	## Handoff relocation rule
32	
33	Write the contract (`status: success`, `handoff_action: implement`, `handoff_output_path: ./progress.md`) **before** invoking `implement`. `implement` may archive the package into `.dev/tasks/done/<id>/`, including when it errors after the move. Afterwards resolve the package by id; a contract rewrite (to `partial`) is allowed only while the package is still at `.dev/tasks/to-do/<id>/`. If only `done/<id>` exists, never write, recreate a directory, or "fix" the contract: the archived contract stays as written, the outcome goes to chat with the actual path. If both locations exist, mutate neither and report the conflict. Contract links stay package-relative `./` and the status of a valid plan stays non-failed.
34	
35	A failed *generation* (no valid plan) and a failed *execution handoff* (valid plan) are different states: never mark a valid gated plan `failed`, never mark a failed generation `success`/`partial`.
36	
37	## When no contract is written
38	
39	STOPs before the package exists (`E-NO-SOURCE`, `E-EMPTY-SOURCE`, `E-LEGACY` including retired `--output`, `E-BAD-FLAG`, `E-PACKAGE-COLLISION`): chat only — **no package directory, no yaml**.
40	
41	After the package exists: any STOP → write the `failed` contract; delete a draft `<id>.md` that failed the gate.
42	
43	## Worker contract (`--unattended`)
44	
45	Written to `<report-dir>/return-contract.yaml` (the one directory passed with `--report-dir`, never the package) on every outcome. The package contract above is unchanged.
46	
47	```yaml
48	worker_contract_version: "1"
49	worker_status: succeeded | partial | failed
50	command: <the exact command line>
51	report_path: <repo path of the plan <id>.md, in to-do/ or, after an archive, done/> | null
52	artifacts: [<package return-contract.yaml>, <package source.md if written>, <each file reflect wrote in its <report-dir>/nested/reflect-<n>/ run directory, whatever reflect_status is>, <docs/memory/reflect/deviation-patterns-<slug>.md if reflect wrote it>]   # [] before a package exists; gitignored .dev/reflect/runs.jsonl and .superclaude/memory/ are left out (WC-4 in ~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md)
53	                                                                    # artifacts also lists the nested reflect contract <report-dir>/nested/reflect-<n>/return-contract.yaml, also when the call failed
54	reason: <the STOP code or the failure>                              # only when failed
55	```
56	
57	Status mapping: package `success` → `succeeded`, `partial` → `partial`, `failed` → `failed`. A pre-creation STOP → `failed` with the STOP code in `reason` and `report_path: null`. A skipped `--handoff implement` makes the package contract `partial` with one `unresolved` line.

1	# CODEGRAPH.md - codegraph usage rules for IronClaude primitives
2	
3	Read this file when a command, skill or agent uses codegraph. It is not loaded into every session. Primitives point here with one line and never copy these rules.
4	
5	## 1. What it is
6	
7	codegraph is a read-only code graph of the current git worktree: symbols, call edges, file outlines and impact, kept as one SQLite index per worktree in `<worktree>/.codegraph/` (gitignored). Markdown, files over 1 MB, ignored files and dependency folders are not indexed. A graph answer locates code; it is never a citation.
8	
9	## 2. Readiness check (once per run)
10	
11	1. Switch: `printenv SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_PRIMITIVES` prints `off` → `index_state: disabled`, `access: none`, token `graph:disabled`; use the Phase 1 floor (Grep, Glob, Read) and stop the check.
12	2. Worktree: `worktree_root` = realpath of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; pass it as `projectPath` on every MCP call.
13	3. MCP detection: read the session's own tool list, never the kind of run. `mcp__codegraph__codegraph_status` listed → call it once with `projectPath`; before that call, when the primitive's Bash allowlist permits `pgrep` and `pgrep -f 'codegraph\.js (init|index)'` prints a line, wait for that build to end (poll up to 60 s); if it is still running after 60 s, skip `status`, set `index_state: stale` and token `graph:stale`. Not listed → CLI `codegraph status` in `worktree_root`, and only when `pgrep -f 'codegraph\.js (init|index)'` prints nothing; when it prints a line, skip `status`, set `index_state: stale` and token `graph:stale` (an init is running; CLI `status` during an init can empty the index).
14	4. Version: `codegraph --version` must equal the pin below; otherwise CLI access is `none` (`graph:absent` when the command is missing, `graph:version_mismatch` plus `graph:provenance_unproven` when it differs, `graph:provenance_unproven` when it cannot be read). MCP access is not affected.
15	5. Classify the status answer into `index_state: fresh|stale|not_initialized|foreign_index|absent|disabled|error`:
16	   - "belongs to a different git working tree" → `foreign_index`, `graph:foreign_index` (a nested worktree answering from its parent's index);
17	   - CLI "Not initialized", or MCP "isn't indexed with codegraph" → `not_initialized`, `graph:not_initialized`;
18	   - CLI "Index is up to date", or MCP "Changes since index: 0 added, 0 modified, 0 removed" → `fresh`;
19	   - a CLI "Pending Changes:" list, or non-zero MCP change counts → `stale`, `graph:stale`;
20	   - no binary and no MCP tool → `absent`, `graph:absent`; anything else → `error`, `graph:parse_failed`.
21	6. Access: lookup tools (`codegraph_search`, `codegraph_callers`, ...) listed → `access: mcp`. Only `codegraph_status` listed → token `graph:unlisted`; then `access: cli` for a primitive whose allowlist names the CLI read verbs and whose `codegraph --version` matches the pin, else `access: none` and the Phase 1 floor (or artifacts the orchestrator put in the brief).
22	7. Record `checked_at` (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`) from one `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` (Bash) run right after the status call, because the status answer has no timestamp; when step 3 skips `status` (a build still running after 60 s, or the CLI guard), take it the same way at the moment the skip is decided, so the `Codegraph` / `Grounding` line always carries a timestamp. Re-check after any write in the same run: no primitive syncs the index (see Never), so rows about files the run changed are leads only.
23	
24	Agents get the run's state in their brief: `index_state`, `checked_at`, `worktree_root` and the `projectPath` to pass; they call codegraph only when `index_state: fresh`.
25	
26	Who indexes: Phase 2's SessionStart hook starts `codegraph init --yes` in every new checkout (switch it off with `SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_AUTOINIT=0`); the main session may run `codegraph init --yes` as the codegraph block of `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` says; among primitives only the user-typed `/sc:graph init` runs `init`. Switches: `SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_PRIMITIVES=off` switches off codegraph use in primitives only; `SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_AUTOINIT=0` switches off only the session-start index hook.
27	
28	## 3. Degraded tokens (closed list; invent none)
29	
30	`graph:absent`, `graph:unlisted`, `graph:disabled`, `graph:not_initialized`, `graph:foreign_index`, `graph:stale`, `graph:version_mismatch`, `graph:provenance_unproven`, `graph:empty`, `graph:ambiguous`, `graph:truncated`, `graph:parse_failed`, `graph:unresolved`, `graph:telemetry_on`.
31	
32	Add the matching token to the host primitive's existing `degraded` / `degraded_components` list and continue on the floor; no token stops a run. A single lookup that fails or returns nothing records `graph:empty` the same way (`graph:truncated` for a caller list shorter than its total, `graph:unresolved` for a row you could not confirm); no new token is added. For `graph:not_initialized` tell the user: run `/sc:graph status`; it reports `next_action: run_graph_init`. `graph:disabled` means the user set `SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_PRIMITIVES=off`.
33	
34	Pinned codegraph version: 1.6.2
35	Freshness experiment E-1: outcome-A
36	
37	E-1 outcome A: CLI `status` lists pending files right after a write even with no MCP server running, so a stale index is detectable; graph rows are still leads only until confirmed (rule 1).
38	
39	## 4. Tool table
40	
41	| Job | MCP tool (seven-tool branch) | CLI form (status-only branch, orchestrators that allow it) |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| Where is X defined | `codegraph_search {query, kind?, limit}` | `codegraph query <name> --json --limit <n>` |
44	| Symbol body, or disambiguate | `codegraph_node {symbol, file?, includeCode:true}` | `codegraph node <name> --file <path>` |
45	| File outline | `codegraph_node {file, symbolsOnly:true}` | `codegraph node --file <path> --symbols-only` |
46	| Diff hunk → enclosing declaration | `codegraph_node {file, line}` | `codegraph query <name> --json` spans (`startLine`, `endLine`) |
47	| Who calls X | `codegraph_callers {symbol, file?, limit}` | `codegraph callers <name> --json --limit <n>` |
48	| What X calls | `codegraph_callees {symbol, file?, limit}` | `codegraph callees <name> --json --limit <n>` |
49	| Impact before an edit | `codegraph_impact {symbol, file?, depth}` | `codegraph impact <name> --depth <n> --json` |
50	| Overview (set `path` to the target's directory when the target is narrower than the repo) | `codegraph_files {format:"grouped", maxDepth:2, path?}` | none |
51	| Readiness | `codegraph_status {projectPath}` | guarded `codegraph status` (section 2) |
52	| Tests affected by changed files | none | `codegraph affected <files...> --json --quiet` (files as arguments; advisory) |
53	
54	Status-only branch: Phase 2 may register only `codegraph_status`; then lookups use the CLI column (where the allowlist names it) or the Phase 1 floor. Other allowed CLI verbs: `codegraph --version`, `codegraph telemetry status`. `codegraph node` has no `--json`. Allowlists name one exact pattern per verb, for example `Bash(codegraph callers *)`.
55	
56	## 5. Standing rules
57	
58	Caller rows give the caller's definition line, not the call site. Before citing one, confirm the call site:
59	
60	1. CS1: find the caller's span (`codegraph query <caller> --json` `startLine`/`endLine`, or `codegraph_node {symbol}`); none → `resolution: unresolved`.
61	2. CS2: Grep `(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_$])<callee>\s*\(` (the name regex-escaped, `$` as `\$`; `\b` cannot sit beside a `$`) with line numbers in that file and keep matches inside the span. Direct callers only: a transitive (`hop` 2) row has no call to `<callee>` and keeps `resolution: def-line`.
62	3. CS3: reject matches in comments, strings or docstrings, bare assignments and attribute-only uses.
63	4. CS4: Read the matched line; it must still hold the call → `resolution: call-site-verified`.
64	5. CS5: any failure drops the row from cited output; never repair it. At most 5 rows per symbol and 20 per run; every row carries `resolution: def-line|call-site-verified|unresolved`.
65	
66	Rules for every primitive:
67	
68	1. Read before cite or edit: re-Read a `file:line` range before quoting it and before any Edit; `codegraph_node` file mode only with `symbolsOnly:true`.
69	2. Fail open to the Phase 1 floor: codegraph missing, unlisted, not initialized, foreign or stale → Grep/Glob/Read, plus one token from section 3.
70	3. Empty is not absence: no "no callers", "no dependents" or "no tests" conclusion comes from a graph result; callers are call edges only.
71	4. Agents get exact names (`mcp__codegraph__codegraph_<tool>`, never a wildcard) and the run's state in the brief (section 2).
72	5. No mutating verb in a skill or agent, and no wildcard allowlist (see Never).
73	6. Both tool-list branches: the same primitive text works whether Phase 2 registered seven tools or only `codegraph_status` (section 4).
74	7. Guard every CLI `status` with `pgrep -f 'codegraph\.js (init|index)'` (skip it while one runs); the MCP `codegraph_status` takes the bounded wait of section 2 step 3 instead.
75	8. Call the CLI as bare `codegraph` (what exact allowlist patterns match); Phase 2's pointer `~/.codegraph/.superclaude-bin` is for the hook and the main session.

# CODEGRAPH.md - codegraph usage rules for IronClaude primitives

Read this file when a command, skill or agent uses codegraph. It is not loaded into every session. Primitives point here with one line and never copy these rules.

## 1. What it is

codegraph is a read-only code graph of the current git worktree: symbols, call edges, file outlines and impact, kept as one SQLite index per worktree in `<worktree>/.codegraph/` (gitignored). Markdown, files over 1 MB, ignored files and dependency folders are not indexed. A graph answer locates code; it is never a citation.

## 2. Readiness check (once per run)

1. Switch: `printenv SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_PRIMITIVES` prints `off` → `index_state: disabled`, `access: none`, token `graph:disabled`; use the Phase 1 floor (Grep, Glob, Read) and stop the check.
2. Worktree: `worktree_root` = realpath of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; pass it as `projectPath` on every MCP call.
3. MCP detection: read the session's own tool list, never the kind of run. `mcp__codegraph__codegraph_status` listed → call it once with `projectPath`; before that call, when the primitive's Bash allowlist permits `pgrep` and `pgrep -f 'codegraph\.js (init|index)'` prints a line, wait for that build to end (poll up to 60 s); if it is still running after 60 s, skip `status`, set `index_state: stale` and token `graph:stale`. Not listed → CLI `codegraph status` in `worktree_root`, and only when `pgrep -f 'codegraph\.js (init|index)'` prints nothing; when it prints a line, skip `status`, set `index_state: stale` and token `graph:stale` (an init is running; CLI `status` during an init can empty the index).
4. Version: `codegraph --version` must equal the pin below; otherwise CLI access is `none` (`graph:absent` when the command is missing, `graph:version_mismatch` plus `graph:provenance_unproven` when it differs, `graph:provenance_unproven` when it cannot be read). MCP access is not affected.
5. Classify the status answer into `index_state: fresh|stale|not_initialized|foreign_index|absent|disabled|error`:
   - "belongs to a different git working tree" → `foreign_index`, `graph:foreign_index` (a nested worktree answering from its parent's index);
   - CLI "Not initialized", or MCP "isn't indexed with codegraph" → `not_initialized`, `graph:not_initialized`;
   - CLI "Index is up to date", or MCP "Changes since index: 0 added, 0 modified, 0 removed" → `fresh`;
   - a CLI "Pending Changes:" list, or non-zero MCP change counts → `stale`, `graph:stale`;
   - no binary and no MCP tool → `absent`, `graph:absent`; anything else → `error`, `graph:parse_failed`.
6. Access: lookup tools (`codegraph_search`, `codegraph_callers`, ...) listed → `access: mcp`. Only `codegraph_status` listed → token `graph:unlisted`; then `access: cli` for a primitive whose allowlist names the CLI read verbs and whose `codegraph --version` matches the pin, else `access: none` and the Phase 1 floor (or artifacts the orchestrator put in the brief).
7. Record `checked_at` (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`) from one `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` (Bash) run right after the status call, because the status answer has no timestamp; when step 3 skips `status` (a build still running after 60 s, or the CLI guard), take it the same way at the moment the skip is decided, so the `Codegraph` / `Grounding` line always carries a timestamp. Re-check after any write in the same run: no primitive syncs the index (see Never), so rows about files the run changed are leads only.

Agents get the run's state in their brief: `index_state`, `checked_at`, `worktree_root` and the `projectPath` to pass; they call codegraph only when `index_state: fresh`.

Who indexes: Phase 2's SessionStart hook starts `codegraph init --yes` in every new checkout (switch it off with `SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_AUTOINIT=0`); the main session may run `codegraph init --yes` as the codegraph block of `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` says; among primitives only the user-typed `/sc:graph init` runs `init`. Switches: `SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_PRIMITIVES=off` switches off codegraph use in primitives only; `SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_AUTOINIT=0` switches off only the session-start index hook.

## 3. Degraded tokens (closed list; invent none)

`graph:absent`, `graph:unlisted`, `graph:disabled`, `graph:not_initialized`, `graph:foreign_index`, `graph:stale`, `graph:version_mismatch`, `graph:provenance_unproven`, `graph:empty`, `graph:ambiguous`, `graph:truncated`, `graph:parse_failed`, `graph:unresolved`, `graph:telemetry_on`.

Add the matching token to the host primitive's existing `degraded` / `degraded_components` list and continue on the floor; no token stops a run. A single lookup that fails or returns nothing records `graph:empty` the same way (`graph:truncated` for a caller list shorter than its total, `graph:unresolved` for a row you could not confirm); no new token is added. For `graph:not_initialized` tell the user: run `/sc:graph status`; it reports `next_action: run_graph_init`. `graph:disabled` means the user set `SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_PRIMITIVES=off`.

Pinned codegraph version: 1.6.2
Freshness experiment E-1: outcome-A

E-1 outcome A: CLI `status` lists pending files right after a write even with no MCP server running, so a stale index is detectable; graph rows are still leads only until confirmed (rule 1).

## 4. Tool table

| Job | MCP tool (seven-tool branch) | CLI form (status-only branch, orchestrators that allow it) |
|---|---|---|
| Where is X defined | `codegraph_search {query, kind?, limit}` | `codegraph query <name> --json --limit <n>` |
| Symbol body, or disambiguate | `codegraph_node {symbol, file?, includeCode:true}` | `codegraph node <name> --file <path>` |
| File outline | `codegraph_node {file, symbolsOnly:true}` | `codegraph node --file <path> --symbols-only` |
| Diff hunk → enclosing declaration | `codegraph_node {file, line}` | `codegraph query <name> --json` spans (`startLine`, `endLine`) |
| Who calls X | `codegraph_callers {symbol, file?, limit}` | `codegraph callers <name> --json --limit <n>` |
| What X calls | `codegraph_callees {symbol, file?, limit}` | `codegraph callees <name> --json --limit <n>` |
| Impact before an edit | `codegraph_impact {symbol, file?, depth}` | `codegraph impact <name> --depth <n> --json` |
| Overview (set `path` to the target's directory when the target is narrower than the repo) | `codegraph_files {format:"grouped", maxDepth:2, path?}` | none |
| Readiness | `codegraph_status {projectPath}` | guarded `codegraph status` (section 2) |
| Tests affected by changed files | none | `codegraph affected <files...> --json --quiet` (files as arguments; advisory) |

Status-only branch: Phase 2 may register only `codegraph_status`; then lookups use the CLI column (where the allowlist names it) or the Phase 1 floor. Other allowed CLI verbs: `codegraph --version`, `codegraph telemetry status`. `codegraph node` has no `--json`. Allowlists name one exact pattern per verb, for example `Bash(codegraph callers *)`.

## 5. Standing rules

Caller rows give the caller's definition line, not the call site. Before citing one, confirm the call site:

1. CS1: find the caller's span (`codegraph query <caller> --json` `startLine`/`endLine`, or `codegraph_node {symbol}`); none → `resolution: unresolved`.
2. CS2: Grep `(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_$])<callee>\s*\(` (the name regex-escaped, `$` as `\$`; `\b` cannot sit beside a `$`) with line numbers in that file and keep matches inside the span. Direct callers only: a transitive (`hop` 2) row has no call to `<callee>` and keeps `resolution: def-line`.
3. CS3: reject matches in comments, strings or docstrings, bare assignments and attribute-only uses.
4. CS4: Read the matched line; it must still hold the call → `resolution: call-site-verified`.
5. CS5: any failure drops the row from cited output; never repair it. At most 5 rows per symbol and 20 per run; every row carries `resolution: def-line|call-site-verified|unresolved`.

Rules for every primitive:

1. Read before cite or edit: re-Read a `file:line` range before quoting it and before any Edit; `codegraph_node` file mode only with `symbolsOnly:true`.
2. Fail open to the Phase 1 floor: codegraph missing, unlisted, not initialized, foreign or stale → Grep/Glob/Read, plus one token from section 3.
3. Empty is not absence: no "no callers", "no dependents" or "no tests" conclusion comes from a graph result; callers are call edges only.
4. Agents get exact names (`mcp__codegraph__codegraph_<tool>`, never a wildcard) and the run's state in the brief (section 2).
5. No mutating verb in a skill or agent, and no wildcard allowlist (see Never).
6. Both tool-list branches: the same primitive text works whether Phase 2 registered seven tools or only `codegraph_status` (section 4).
7. Guard every CLI `status` with `pgrep -f 'codegraph\.js (init|index)'` (skip it while one runs); the MCP `codegraph_status` takes the bounded wait of section 2 step 3 instead.
8. Call the CLI as bare `codegraph` (what exact allowlist patterns match); Phase 2's pointer `~/.codegraph/.superclaude-bin` is for the hook and the main session.
9. Tier above the floor: a codegraph step goes before the existing Grep/Read step, which stays unchanged; never "skip" where a floor exists.

## 6. Known gaps and fallbacks

- No text search (names only) → Grep. No diagnostics or type checker → the project's own tools through Bash in the orchestrator. No type hierarchy and no implementations tool → `codegraph_search {kind:"class"}` candidates confirmed by Grep and Read. No edits → Read then Edit/Write. No memory.
- Caller lists show 20 rows by default: record `shown/total`, re-query once with a limit up to 100, else `graph:truncated`.
- Dependency folders are not indexed → Read the installed package source or use Context7; else mark the claim `[INFERRED]`.
- The index catches up only while a codegraph MCP server watches the worktree (E-1); otherwise it stays behind until the next sync.

## 7. Never

The only section that names these:

- Call `codegraph_explore`, `codegraph explore` or `codegraph context`.
- Use `codegraph_node` file mode without `symbolsOnly:true`.
- Run CLI `codegraph status` while an init or index is running.
- From a skill or agent, run `codegraph init` (only the user-typed `/sc:graph init` does).
- Run `codegraph install`, `codegraph upgrade`, `codegraph uninstall`, `codegraph uninit`, `codegraph index`, `codegraph sync`, `codegraph unlock`, `codegraph telemetry on|off` or `codegraph prompt-hook` (Phase 2 owns install; no primitive syncs the index).
- Write `Bash(codegraph *)` or `mcp__codegraph__*` in an allowlist.
- Prefix a call with environment variables (`VAR=1 codegraph ...` defeats per-verb allowlist matching; E-3).

1	"""ledger-v1 reader, the four row checks, linking, demotion, telemetry and promotion (DESIGN 9.1 to 9.4, DD-2, DD-3,
2	DD-9, DD-11, DD-12).
3	
4	    read_ledger(report, assigned)   the `## Ledger` block of a reviewer's final message as rows, with every format
5	                                    problem counted (DESIGN 9.1)
6	    Corpora / transcript_results    the four places a `quote_other` may come from (DD-2)
7	    check_report(report, ...)       reader + checks 1 to 4 (9.2) + linking + demotion + `class` telemetry + promotion
8	                                    (9.3) for one reviewer; returns the checked text (the raw report is never edited)
9	                                    and every count
10	    summarise(results)              the per-run check.json of DESIGN 9.4 from the per-reviewer results
11	    carries_cb3(...)                the CB-3 sentence rule
12	
13	Findings parsing comes only from scaffold/fnd.py; the telemetry keys and the per-class tables are in scaffold/telemetry.py.
14	
15	Gaps in DESIGN 9.3 and 9.4 resolved by Task 25 (each is a choice the design leaves open; every one is covered by a test):
16	  P1  Promotion id. `P<item>`; when that id is already in the block the one suffix `-2` is tried (`PS3-2`; a plain
17	      digit would make `PS3` + `2` collide with the promoted line of an item `S32`), and a second collision is a
18	      duplicate id, so `_check_finding` rejects it and the row is a promotion failure. A reviewer has at most one
19	      row per item (`dup_line`), so a second collision means the reviewer used both ids itself.
20	  P2  A promoted line is checked with `fnd._check_finding` first and its message is the logged reason. Then two
21	      conditions the design states elsewhere are added to the same list of failures: the row broke a ledger limit
22	      (9.1 item 5: "cannot be promoted") and the `problem` is empty (the check never writes a claim of its own, so an
23	      empty claim is not promoted). An empty `quote_plan` is refused by `_check_finding` itself (anchor minimum).
24	      A row of an item with no `class` in items.json, or of a class with no card, is also a failure (no category).
25	      Every failure is logged `{item, id, reason}`; none is silent.
26	  P3  Promotion asks for no support: the design (9.3) gives the PROBLEM verdict and "no linked findings line" as the
27	      only conditions. A promoted anchor is the row's `quote_plan` as written, found in the candidate or not.
28	  P4  "Linked" for promotion means the finding links to the row by probe or by quote, whether or not the row is
29	      OK, and whether or not the finding line itself is a valid findings line. A broken row (a format error line) is
30	      not in `rows`, so it is never promoted.
31	  P5  Telemetry: `class` is written on every linked line whose item has a class in items.json (added when missing,
32	      corrected when different), also on an OK-row line and on a line that stays blocking. The reviewer's `probe` is
33	      kept as written and none is added to a quote-linked line. A line is rewritten (`json.dumps`, the line ending
34	      kept) only when `blocking` or `class` changes; an untouched line keeps its bytes. Corrections are counted in
35	      `class_corrected`, additions in `class_added` (DESIGN 9.4 has no field for them; they are extra keys of check.json).
36	  P6  The unusable block: nothing is promoted and no line is touched (G10); `block_unusable` carries the reason in the
37	      per-reviewer result and the reviewer id in check.json.
38	  P7  check.json extras beyond the DESIGN 9.4 fields: `reviewer_findings` (the findings lines read, so promoted ones are
39	      counted apart), `demoted_findings`, `class_added`, `class_corrected`, `per_class` and `no_report` (a reviewer
40	      with no report file). `missing_line` lists only reviewers whose ledger was read; a `ledger_missing` reviewer is
41	      under `ledger_missing` alone.
42	
43	Gaps in DESIGN 9 resolved here (each is a choice the design leaves open; every one is covered by a test):
44	  G1  `corpus` is the FIRST match in the order of DD-2: source, candidate, sheet, transcript. A quote that is also in
45	      the transcript only because the reviewer read the candidate (nearly every run) is therefore `candidate`, not
46	      `transcript`, so a row whose two quotes are the same plan text cannot pass as a "search result". Consequence:
47	      a `sheet` or `transcript` match is never in the candidate, so it always differs from the plan quote and
48	      `search_supported` implies `quotes_supported`; the flag is kept because 9.2 check 4 defines it.
49	  G2  Sheet corpus (9.2 check 3, "a printed tool line of this item"): the evidence `text` of the row's item, and the
50	      same entry in its printed form (`plan line 85: <text>`, `<path>:12: <text>`; render.py's form).
51	  G3  Transcript corpus: the string `content` of every `tool_result` block of every `user` event (a list of `text`
52	      parts is joined per part). One block is one corpus entry: a quote cannot span two tool results. Nothing
53	      from `assistant` events is read here. Real files: results/transcript-shapes.md.
54	  G4  Where the ledger is looked for (9.1 items 1 and 2). `findings_heading_missing` (no `## Findings block`, so no
55	      span), `ledger_heading_missing`, `ledger_after_findings` (every `## Ledger` heading is below the findings
56	      heading), `heading_between` (another heading, outside code fences, sits between the two), `no_block`,
57	      `two_blocks` (counted over the whole report, so a stray block before the heading also counts), `unclosed`
58	      (the fence never closes, or it swallows the findings heading) and `block_outside_span`. Each is
59	      `ledger_missing` and leaves no rows. The last `## Ledger` heading above the findings heading is the one used.
60	  G5  A line that is a format error but names an assigned item (`"item": "S2"` is read from the object, or from the
61	      text by a regular expression when the JSON is broken) makes that item `broken`, unless a good row for it
62	      exists. A finding linked to a broken row gets the cause `row_missing`. An item with no line at all is in
63	      `missing_line` and is NOT a broken row; a finding whose probe names it is not linked to anything (there is no
64	      row) unless its anchor contains another row's `quote_plan`.
65	  G6  Quote linking needs a `quote_plan` of at least 12 flattened characters (the schema floor), so a three-letter
66	      quote cannot link every finding.
67	  G7  A finding that would be demoted for more than one cause counts every cause that holds in `demoted`, and once
68	      in `demoted_findings`. `format_induced` is true only when every cause is format-induced: `row_missing`, or
69	      `row_unsupported` where `problem` and both quotes are present and a quote test failed.
70	  G8  A linked finding whose row is `OK` is left alone whatever its blocking flag (DESIGN 9.3, "left alone"); it is
71	      counted as `ok_but_finding` whether or not it is blocking.
72	  G9  `CHECK_SCOPE=all` (never used in an arm): an unlinked blocking finding is held to the same rule with its own
73	      `anchor` and `anchor2` as the two quotes: `anchor` must be in the candidate, `anchor2` must be in one of the
74	      four corpora (the sheet corpus is then every item's tool lines), and the two must differ, or `anchor2` is a
75	      sheet or transcript match. Causes are `row_unsupported` and `no_cb3`.
76	  G10 When the findings block is unusable (missing, unclosed or duplicated; DESIGN 9.3 "Block repair is out of scope")
77	      the text comes back unchanged and `block_unusable` names the reason; rows are still read and checked.
78	  G11 `CB-3` window: the sentence counts when it lies within 12 lines above or below a line that holds the finding
79	      id as a whole word, in the report text above the `## Findings block` heading. Lines are joined and flattened
80	      first, so a sentence wrapped over two lines still counts.
81	  Not resolved (the design gives no number): `quote_other` has no minimum length, so a very short second quote
82	  passes check 3 if it occurs anywhere in a corpus.
83	"""
84	
85	from __future__ import annotations
86	
87	import json
88	import os
89	import re
90	from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence
91	from pathlib import Path
92	
93	from scaffold import cards as cards_mod
94	from scaffold import fnd, telemetry
95	
96	HEAD_LEDGER = re.compile(r"^#{1,6}\s+Ledger\s*$", re.M | re.I)
97	_HEADING_LINE = re.compile(r"^#{1,6}\s+\S")
98	_FENCE_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s{0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})\s*([^`\s]*)\s*$")
99	_ITEM_TEXT = re.compile(r'"item"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"')
100	
101	CB3_SENTENCE = "An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds"
102	VERDICTS = ("OK", "PROBLEM", "UNSURE")
103	CAUSES = ("row_unsupported", "row_unsure", "no_cb3", "row_missing")
104	SCOPES = ("linked", "all")
105	CORPORA = ("source", "candidate", "sheet", "transcript")
106	QUOTE_PLAN_MIN = 12
107	QUOTE_PLAN_MAX = 200
108	PROBLEM_MAX = 300
109	RAN_MAX_WORDS = 15
110	CB3_WINDOW = 12
111	_TEXT_KEYS = ("quote_plan", "quote_other", "problem", "ran")
112	_CB3_FLAT = fnd.flat(CB3_SENTENCE).lower()
113	
114	
115	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- positions and fences
116	
117	
118	def _line_of(text: str, pos: int) -> int:
119	    """1-based line number of character offset pos."""
120	    return text.count("\n", 0, pos) + 1
121	
122	
123	def _fenced(report: str, info: str) -> list[tuple[int, list[tuple[int, str]], bool]]:
124	    """Every fenced block of the whole report with this info string, like fnd._blocks_after but not tied to a heading.
125	
126	    A one-line heading is put in front of the text so the scan starts at the first real line; the numbers it returns
127	    are shifted back, so they are lines of `report`.
128	    """
129	    _, blocks = fnd._blocks_after("#\n" + report, re.compile(r"^#\n", re.M), info)
130	    return [
131	        (s - 1, [(n - 1, t) for n, t in body], closed) for s, body, closed in blocks
132	    ]
133	
134	
135	def _heading_between(lines: list[str], first: int, last: int) -> bool:
136	    """True when a heading line outside a code fence sits on a line strictly between `first` and `last` (1-based)."""
137	    marker: str | None = None
138	    for n in range(first + 1, last):
139	        line = lines[n - 1]
140	        fm = _FENCE_LINE.match(line)
141	        if marker is None:
142	            if fm:
143	                marker = fm.group(1)
144	            elif _HEADING_LINE.match(line):
145	                return True
146	        elif (
147	            fm
148	            and not fm.group(2)
149	            and fm.group(1)[0] == marker[0]
150	            and len(fm.group(1)) >= len(marker)
151	        ):
152	            marker = None
153	    return False
154	
155	
156	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 9.1 the reader
157	
158	
159	def _recover_item(raw: str, obj: object) -> str | None:
160	    if isinstance(obj, dict) and isinstance(obj.get("item"), str):
161	        return obj["item"].strip() or None
162	    m = _ITEM_TEXT.search(raw)
163	    return m.group(1).strip() if m else None
164	
165	
166	def read_ledger(report: str, assigned: Sequence[str]) -> dict:
167	    """The ledger of a final message (DESIGN 9.1) as a dict.
168	
169	    {"ledger_missing": bool, "reason": str | None, "rows": [row], "format_errors": [{line, msg}],
170	     "normalised_verdict": n, "dup_line": [{line, item}], "unknown_item": [{line, item}],
171	     "broken_items": [item], "missing_line": [item]}
172	
173	    A row is {item, verdict, quote_plan, quote_other, problem, ran, line, limits_violated: [name]}. The verdict is
174	    upper-cased and trimmed. Rows come back in the order of the lines. When `ledger_missing` is true `rows` is empty and
175	    `missing_line` holds every assigned item.
176	    """
177	    assigned = list(assigned)
178	    res: dict = {
179	        "ledger_missing": True,
180	        "reason": None,
181	        "rows": [],
182	        "format_errors": [],
183	        "normalised_verdict": 0,
184	        "dup_line": [],
185	        "unknown_item": [],
186	        "broken_items": [],
187	        "missing_line": list(assigned),
188	    }
189	    fm = fnd._HEAD_FINDINGS.search(report)
190	    if not fm:
191	        res["reason"] = "findings_heading_missing"
192	        return res
193	    f_line = _line_of(report, fm.start())
194	    heads = [_line_of(report, m.start()) for m in HEAD_LEDGER.finditer(report)]
195	    above = [h for h in heads if h < f_line]
196	    if not above:
197	        res["reason"] = "ledger_after_findings" if heads else "ledger_heading_missing"
198	        return res
199	    l_line = above[-1]
200	    if _heading_between(report.splitlines(), l_line, f_line):
201	        res["reason"] = "heading_between"
202	        return res
203	    blocks = _fenced(report, "ledger-v1")
204	    if not blocks:
205	        res["reason"] = "no_block"
206	        return res
207	    if len(blocks) > 1:
208	        res["reason"] = "two_blocks"
209	        return res
210	    start, body, closed = blocks[0]
211	    if not l_line < start < f_line:
212	        res["reason"] = "block_outside_span"
213	        return res
214	    if not closed or (body and body[-1][0] >= f_line):
215	        res["reason"] = "unclosed"
216	        return res
217	    res["ledger_missing"] = False
218	
219	    by_item: dict[str, dict] = {}
220	    broken: dict[str, int] = {}
221	
222	    def error(lineno: int, msg: str, item: str | None) -> None:
223	        res["format_errors"].append({"line": lineno, "msg": msg})
224	        if item and item in assigned:
225	            broken.setdefault(item, lineno)
226	
227	    for lineno, raw in body:
228	        if not raw.strip():
229	            continue
230	        try:
231	            obj = json.loads(raw)
232	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
233	            error(lineno, f"not valid JSON: {exc.msg}", _recover_item(raw, None))
234	            continue
235	        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
236	            error(lineno, "a line must be a JSON object", None)
237	            continue
238	        item, verdict = obj.get("item"), obj.get("verdict")
239	        known = _recover_item(raw, obj)
240	        if not isinstance(item, str) or not item.strip():
241	            error(lineno, "item is missing or not a string", known)
242	            continue
243	        if not isinstance(verdict, str):
244	            error(lineno, "verdict is missing or not a string", known)
245	            continue
246	        canon = verdict.strip().upper()
247	        if canon not in VERDICTS:
248	            error(lineno, "verdict must be OK, PROBLEM or UNSURE", known)
249	            continue
250	        values = {k: ("" if obj.get(k) is None else obj[k]) for k in _TEXT_KEYS}
251	        bad = [k for k, v in values.items() if not isinstance(v, str)]
252	        if bad:
253	            error(lineno, f"{', '.join(bad)} must be a string", known)
254	            continue
255	        if canon != verdict:
256	            res["normalised_verdict"] += 1
257	        item = item.strip()
258	        if item not in assigned:
259	            res["unknown_item"].append({"line": lineno, "item": item})
260	            continue
261	        if item in by_item:
262	            res["dup_line"].append({"line": lineno, "item": item})
263	            continue
264	        limits = []
265	        qp = fnd.flat(values["quote_plan"])
266	        if qp and not QUOTE_PLAN_MIN <= len(qp) <= QUOTE_PLAN_MAX:
267	            limits.append("quote_plan")
268	        if len(fnd.flat(values["problem"])) > PROBLEM_MAX:
269	            limits.append("problem")
270	        if len(values["ran"].split()) > RAN_MAX_WORDS:
271	            limits.append("ran")
272	        by_item[item] = {
273	            "item": item,
274	            "verdict": canon,
275	            **values,
276	            "line": lineno,
277	            "limits_violated": limits,
278	        }
279	        res["rows"].append(by_item[item])
280	    res["broken_items"] = [i for i in assigned if i in broken and i not in by_item]
281	    res["missing_line"] = [
282	        i for i in assigned if i not in by_item and i not in res["broken_items"]
283	    ]
284	    return res
285	
286	
287	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 9.2 corpora and the four checks
288	
289	
290	def transcript_results(events: object) -> list[str]:
291	    """The tool results of a run transcript (the parsed `*.attempt1.json`): one string per `tool_result` block (G3)."""
292	    out: list[str] = []
293	    if not isinstance(events, list):
294	        return out
295	    for ev in events:
296	        if not isinstance(ev, dict) or ev.get("type") != "user":
297	            continue
298	        message = ev.get("message")
299	        content = message.get("content") if isinstance(message, dict) else None
300	        if not isinstance(content, list):
301	            continue
302	        for block in content:
303	            if not isinstance(block, dict) or block.get("type") != "tool_result":
304	                continue
305	            c = block.get("content")
306	            if isinstance(c, str):
307	                out.append(c)
308	            elif isinstance(c, list):
309	                out += [
310	                    p["text"]
311	                    for p in c
312	                    if isinstance(p, dict)
313	                    and p.get("type") == "text"
314	                    and isinstance(p.get("text"), str)
315	                ]
316	    return out
317	
318	
319	def read_transcript(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
320	    """transcript_results of the JSON file at path."""
321	    return transcript_results(json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
322	
323	
324	def _printed_lines(item: dict) -> list[str]:
325	    """The tool lines of an item as the reader of the sheet sees them (G2): the entry text, and its printed form."""
326	    out = []
327	    for e in item.get("evidence") or []:
328	        text = e.get("text", "")
329	        out.append(text)
330	        path, line = e.get("path"), e.get("line")
331	        if line and path in ("plan", "source"):
332	            out.append(f"{path} line {line}: {text}")
333	        elif line and path:
334	            out.append(f"{path}:{line}: {text}")
335	    return out
336	
337	
338	class Corpora:
339	    """The four places a `quote_other` may come from (DD-2): `source`, `candidate`, `sheet`, `transcript`.
340	
341	    `items` are the item dicts of items.json (`item_id`, `evidence`); `transcript` is a list of tool-result strings.
342	    """
343	
344	    def __init__(
345	        self,
346	        candidate: str,
347	        source: str | None = None,
348	        items: Iterable[dict] = (),
349	        transcript: Iterable[str] = (),
350	    ):
351	        self.candidate = candidate
352	        self.source = source
353	        self._sheet = {
354	            it["item_id"]: [fnd.flat(t) for t in _printed_lines(it)] for it in items
355	        }
356	        self._transcript = [fnd.flat(t) for t in transcript]
357	
358	    def in_candidate(self, quote: str) -> bool:
359	        return bool(fnd.locate(self.candidate, quote))
360	
361	    def find(self, quote: str, item: str | None = None) -> str | None:
362	        """The first corpus, in the order of DD-2, that holds the flattened quote (G1); None when none does.
363	
364	        The sheet corpus is the tool lines of `item`, or of every item when `item` is None.
365	        """
366	        q = fnd.flat(quote)
367	        if not q:
368	            return None
369	        if self.source is not None and fnd.locate(self.source, q):
370	            return "source"
371	        if fnd.locate(self.candidate, q):
372	            return "candidate"
373	        pools = (
374	            self._sheet.get(item, [])
375	            if item is not None
376	            else [t for v in self._sheet.values() for t in v]
377	        )
378	        if any(q in t for t in pools):
379	            return "sheet"
380	        if any(q in t for t in self._transcript):
381	            return "transcript"
382	        return None
383	
384	
385	def _support(plan_ok: bool, other_ok: bool, corpus: str | None, same: bool) -> dict:
386	    quotes = plan_ok and other_ok and not same
387	    search = plan_ok and other_ok and corpus in ("sheet", "transcript")
388	    return {
389	        "quotes_supported": quotes,
390	        "search_supported": search,
391	        "supported": quotes or search,
392	    }
393	
394	
395	def check_row(row: dict, corpora: Corpora) -> dict:
396	    """Checks 2 to 4 of DESIGN 9.2 for one row: the row plus quote_plan_ok, quote_other_ok, corpus and the support flags."""
397	    plan_ok = bool(row["quote_plan"].strip()) and corpora.in_candidate(
398	        row["quote_plan"]
399	    )
400	    corpus = corpora.find(row["quote_other"], row["item"])
401	    same = fnd.flat(row["quote_plan"]) == fnd.flat(row["quote_other"])
402	    return {
403	        **row,
404	        "quote_plan_ok": plan_ok,
405	        "quote_other_ok": corpus is not None,
406	        "corpus": corpus,
407	        **_support(plan_ok, corpus is not None, corpus, same),
408	    }
409	
410	
411	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 9.3 the CB-3 sentence, linking, demotion
412	
413	
414	def carries_cb3(finding: dict, lines_above: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
415	    """True when the finding carries the CB-3 sentence (DESIGN 9.3, G11).
416	
417	    `lines_above` are the report lines above the `## Findings block` heading. The comparison is flattened and
418	    case-insensitive.
419	    """
420	    claim = finding.get("claim")
421	    if isinstance(claim, str) and _CB3_FLAT in fnd.flat(claim).lower():
422	        return True
423	    fid = finding.get("id")
424	    if not isinstance(fid, str):
425	        return False
426	    mention = re.compile(
427	        rf"(?<![A-Za-z0-9._-]){re.escape(fid)}(?![A-Za-z0-9_-]|\.[A-Za-z0-9])"
428	    )
429	    for i, line in enumerate(lines_above):
430	        if mention.search(line):
431	            window = " ".join(lines_above[max(0, i - CB3_WINDOW) : i + CB3_WINDOW + 1])
432	            if _CB3_FLAT in fnd.flat(window).lower():
433	                return True
434	    return False
435	
436	
437	def findings_block_status(report: str) -> tuple[str | None, tuple | None]:
438	    """(reason the block is unusable or None, the block). The block is (fence line, [(line, text)], closed)."""
439	    found, blocks = fnd._blocks_after(report, fnd._HEAD_FINDINGS, "findings-v1")
440	    if not found:
441	        return "findings_heading_missing", None
442	    if not blocks:
443	        return "no_findings_block", None
444	    if len(blocks) > 1:
445	        return "findings_block_duplicated", None
446	    if not blocks[0][2]:
447	        return "findings_block_unclosed", None
448	    return None, blocks[0]
449	
450	
451	def scope_from(scope: str | None = None) -> str:
452	    """`scope`, else the environment variable CHECK_SCOPE, else `linked` (DD-3)."""
453	    value = scope if scope is not None else (os.environ.get("CHECK_SCOPE") or "linked")
454	    if value not in SCOPES:
455	        raise ValueError(f"CHECK_SCOPE must be one of {SCOPES}, not {value!r}")
456	    return value
457

459	def _link(finding: dict, assigned: list[str], rows: dict, broken: list[str], ordered):
460	    """(row or None, how, probe_unknown). `how` is "probe", "quote" or None; a broken row is {"item", "broken": True}."""
461	    probe = finding.get("probe")
462	    unknown = False
463	    if isinstance(probe, str) and probe.strip():
464	        p = probe.strip()
465	        if p not in assigned:
466	            unknown = True
467	        elif p in rows:
468	            return rows[p], "probe", False
469	        elif p in broken:
470	            return {"item": p, "broken": True}, "probe", False
471	    anchor = (
472	        fnd.flat(finding["anchor"]) if isinstance(finding.get("anchor"), str) else ""
473	    )
474	    for row in ordered:
475	        qp = fnd.flat(row["quote_plan"])
476	        if len(qp) >= QUOTE_PLAN_MIN and qp in anchor:
477	            return row, "quote", unknown
478	    return None, None, unknown
479

481	def _own_quotes(finding: dict, corpora: Corpora) -> dict:
482	    """Support of an unlinked finding under CHECK_SCOPE=all (G9): its anchor and anchor2 are the two quotes."""
483	    anchor, anchor2 = finding.get("anchor"), finding.get("anchor2")
484	    plan_ok = isinstance(anchor, str) and corpora.in_candidate(anchor)
485	    corpus = corpora.find(anchor2) if isinstance(anchor2, str) else None
486	    same = fnd.flat(anchor or "") == fnd.flat(anchor2 or "")
487	    return _support(plan_ok, corpus is not None, corpus, same)
488	
489	
490	def _row_causes(row: dict) -> tuple[list[str], bool]:
491	    """(causes, format_induced) for a linked, blocking finding, apart from no_cb3."""
492	    if row.get("broken"):
493	        return ["row_missing"], True
494	    if row["verdict"] == "UNSURE":
495	        return ["row_unsure"], False
496	    if row["verdict"] == "PROBLEM" and not row["supported"]:
497	        fmt = bool(
498	            row["problem"].strip()
499	            and row["quote_plan"].strip()
500	            and row["quote_other"].strip()
501	            and not (row["quote_plan_ok"] and row["quote_other_ok"])
502	        )
503	        return ["row_unsupported"], fmt
504	    return [], False

507	def check_report(
508	    report: str,
509	    *,
510	    assigned: Sequence[str],
511	    candidate: str,
512	    source: str | None = None,
513	    items: Iterable[dict] = (),
514	    transcript: Iterable[str] = (),
515	    scope: str | None = None,
516	    cards: dict[str, dict] | None = None,
517	) -> dict:
518	    """One reviewer's report through the reader, checks 1 to 4, linking, demotion, telemetry and promotion.
519	
520	    `items` are the item dicts of items.json (`item_id`, `class`, `evidence`); the class of an item is where the
521	    `class` key and the promotion category come from (the card of the class, `cards`, default cards/).
522	
523	    Returns {"scope", "ledger": <read_ledger result, rows checked>, "block_unusable": reason | None,
524	    "findings": [per finding: id, line, probe, row_item, link, class, class_change, blocking, demoted, causes,
525	    format_induced, ok_but_finding], "probe_unknown": n, "ok_but_finding": n, "demoted": {cause: n},
526	    "demoted_findings": n, "format_induced_demotions": n, "class_added": n, "class_corrected": n,
527	    "promoted": [{id, item, class, line}], "promotion_failures": [{item, id, reason}], "text": the checked report}.
528	    `text` is `report` with the demotions, the `class` keys and the promoted lines written; it is `report` itself
529	    when the block is unusable or nothing changes. The raw report is never edited.
530	    """
531	    scope = scope_from(scope)
532	    assigned = list(assigned)
533	    items = list(items)
534	    classes = {it["item_id"]: it["class"] for it in items if it.get("class")}
535	    corpora = Corpora(candidate, source, items, list(transcript))
536	    ledger = read_ledger(report, assigned)
537	    ledger["rows"] = [check_row(r, corpora) for r in ledger["rows"]]
538	    rows = {r["item"]: r for r in ledger["rows"]}
539	    out = {
540	        "scope": scope,
541	        "ledger": ledger,
542	        "block_unusable": None,
543	        "findings": [],
544	        "probe_unknown": 0,
545	        "ok_but_finding": 0,
546	        "demoted": dict.fromkeys(CAUSES, 0),
547	        "demoted_findings": 0,
548	        "format_induced_demotions": 0,
549	        "class_added": 0,
550	        "class_corrected": 0,
551	        "promoted": [],
552	        "promotion_failures": [],
553	        "text": report,
554	    }
555	    reason, block = findings_block_status(report)
556	    if reason:
557	        out["block_unusable"] = reason
558	        return out
559	    lines = report.splitlines(keepends=True)
560	    f_line = _line_of(report, fnd._HEAD_FINDINGS.search(report).start())
561	    above = [ln.rstrip("\r\n") for ln in lines[: f_line - 1]]
562	    changed = False
563	    for lineno, raw in block[1]:
564	        try:
565	            obj = json.loads(raw)
566	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
567	            continue
568	        if (
569	            not isinstance(obj, dict)
570	            or "prior" in obj
571	            or not isinstance(obj.get("id"), str)
572	        ):
573	            continue
574	        row, how, unknown = _link(
575	            obj, assigned, rows, ledger["broken_items"], ledger["rows"]
576	        )
577	        out["probe_unknown"] += unknown
578	        item_class = classes.get(row["item"]) if row else None
579	        rec = {
580	            "id": obj["id"],
581	            "line": lineno,
582	            "probe": obj.get("probe"),
583	            "row_item": row["item"] if row else None,
584	            "link": how,
585	            "class": item_class,
586	            "class_change": None,
587	            "blocking": obj.get("blocking") is True,
588	            "demoted": False,
589	            "causes": [],
590	            "format_induced": False,
591	            "ok_but_finding": False,
592	        }
593	        out["findings"].append(rec)
594	        rewrite = False
595	        state = telemetry.fill_class(obj, item_class)  # DD-12 (P5)
596	        if state:
597	            rec["class_change"] = state
598	            out[f"class_{state}"] += 1
599	            rewrite = True
600	        if row is not None and not row.get("broken") and row["verdict"] == "OK":
601	            out["ok_but_finding"] += 1
602	            rec["ok_but_finding"] = True
603	        elif rec["blocking"] and (row is not None or scope == "all"):
604	            if row is not None:
605	                causes, fmt = _row_causes(row)
606	            else:
607	                causes, fmt = (
608	                    (
609	                        []
610	                        if _own_quotes(obj, corpora)["supported"]
611	                        else ["row_unsupported"]
612	                    ),
613	                    False,
614	                )
615	            if not carries_cb3(obj, above):
616	                causes.append("no_cb3")
617	            if causes:
618	                rec.update(
619	                    demoted=True,
620	                    causes=causes,
621	                    format_induced=fmt and "no_cb3" not in causes,
622	                )
623	                for c in causes:
624	                    out["demoted"][c] += 1
625	                out["demoted_findings"] += 1
626	                out["format_induced_demotions"] += rec["format_induced"]
627	                obj["blocking"] = False
628	                rewrite = True
629	        if rewrite:
630	            lines[lineno - 1] = (
631	                json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False) + lines[lineno - 1][len(raw) :]
632	            )
633	            changed = True
634	    linked = {rec["row_item"] for rec in out["findings"] if rec["link"]}
635	    todo = [
636	        r
637	        for r in ledger["rows"]
638	        if r["verdict"] == "PROBLEM" and r["item"] not in linked
639	    ]
640	    if todo:
641	        changed |= _promote(todo, block, lines, classes, cards, out)
642	    if changed:
643	        out["text"] = "".join(lines)
644	    return out
645	
646	
647	def _promotion_line(
648	    row: dict, item_class: str | None, cards: dict | None, seen: set[str]
649	) -> tuple[dict | None, str, str | None]:
650	    """(the promoted line or None, its id, the reason it was refused or None) for one PROBLEM row (DESIGN 9.3, P1, P2)."""
651	    base = f"P{row['item']}"
652	    pid = base if base not in seen else f"{base}-2"
653	    if not item_class:
654	        return (
655	            None,
656	            pid,
657	            "the item has no class in items.json: no category to promote under",
658	        )
659	    try:
660	        category = cards_mod.promote_category(item_class, cards)
661	    except KeyError:
662	        return None, pid, f"no card for class {item_class}"
663	    line = {
664	        "id": pid,
665	        "severity": "MINOR",
666	        "blocking": False,
667	        "category": category,
668	        "anchor": row["quote_plan"],
669	        "refs": [],
670	        "claim": row["problem"],
671	        **telemetry.promoted_keys(row["item"], item_class),
672	    }
673	    err = fnd._check_finding(line, seen)
674	    if err is None and not row["problem"].strip():
675	        err = "problem is empty: the check writes no claim of its own"
676	    if err is None and row["limits_violated"]:
677	        err = "the row breaks a ledger limit: " + ", ".join(row["limits_violated"])
678	    return (None if err else line), pid, err
679	
680	
681	def _promote(
682	    todo: list[dict],
683	    block: tuple,
684	    lines: list[str],
685	    classes: dict[str, str],
686	    cards: dict | None,
687	    out: dict,
688	) -> bool:
689	    """Insert one MINOR, non-blocking line per row of `todo` as the last lines inside the one findings block (9.3).
690	
691	    `lines` (the report with line endings) is edited in place. A refused row goes to out["promotion_failures"] and is
692	    skipped; an inserted one to out["promoted"]. True when a line was inserted.
693	    """
694	    seen: set[str] = set()
695	    for _, raw in block[1]:
696	        try:
697	            obj = json.loads(raw)
698	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
699	            continue
700	        if (
701	            isinstance(obj, dict)
702	            and "prior" not in obj
703	            and isinstance(obj.get("id"), str)
704	        ):
705	            seen.add(obj["id"])
706	    close = block[0] + len(
707	        block[1]
708	    )  # 0-based index of the closing fence: opener line n is index n-1
709	    eol = "\r\n" if lines[close - 1].endswith("\r\n") else "\n"
710	    new: list[str] = []
711	    for row in todo:
712	        item_class = classes.get(row["item"])
713	        line, pid, err = _promotion_line(row, item_class, cards, seen)
714	        if err:
715	            out["promotion_failures"].append(
716	                {"item": row["item"], "id": pid, "reason": err}
717	            )
718	            continue
719	        seen.add(pid)
720	        new.append(json.dumps(line, ensure_ascii=False) + eol)
721	        out["promoted"].append(
722	            {
723	                "id": pid,
724	                "item": row["item"],
725	                "class": item_class,
726	                "line": close + 1 + len(new) - 1,
727	            }
728	        )
729	    lines[close:close] = new
730	    return bool(new)
731	
732	
733	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 9.4 the per-run check.json
734	
735	
736	def summarise(
737	    results: dict[str, dict],
738	    classes: dict[str, str] | None = None,
739	    no_report: Sequence[str] = (),
740	) -> dict:
741	    """check.json of DESIGN 9.4 from {reviewer id: check_report result}, with the extras of P7.
742	
743	    Reviewer findings and promoted findings are counted apart: `reviewer_findings` is the findings lines the
744	    reviewers wrote, `promoted` the lines the check inserted. `classes` is {item id: class} for the per-class tables.
745	    """
746	    out: dict = {
747	        "ledger_missing": [],
748	        "format_errors": 0,
749	        "normalised_verdict": 0,
750	        "dup_line": 0,
751	        "unknown_item": 0,
752	        "probe_unknown": 0,
753	        "missing_line": {},
754	        "rows": dict.fromkeys(VERDICTS, 0),
755	        "demoted": dict.fromkeys(CAUSES, 0),
756	        "format_induced_demotions": 0,
757	        "promoted": 0,
758	        "promotion_failures": [],
759	        "ok_but_finding": 0,
760	        "block_unusable": [],
761	        "reviewer_findings": 0,
762	        "demoted_findings": 0,
763	        "class_added": 0,
764	        "class_corrected": 0,
765	        "per_class": {},
766	        "no_report": list(no_report),
767	    }
768	    for rid, res in results.items():
769	        led = res["ledger"]
770	        if led["ledger_missing"]:
771	            out["ledger_missing"].append(rid)
772	        elif led["missing_line"]:
773	            out["missing_line"][rid] = list(led["missing_line"])
774	        out["format_errors"] += len(led["format_errors"])
775	        out["normalised_verdict"] += led["normalised_verdict"]
776	        out["dup_line"] += len(led["dup_line"])
777	        out["unknown_item"] += len(led["unknown_item"])
778	        for r in led["rows"]:
779	            out["rows"][r["verdict"]] += 1
780	        for c in CAUSES:
781	            out["demoted"][c] += res["demoted"][c]
782	        for k in (
783	            "probe_unknown",
784	            "format_induced_demotions",
785	            "ok_but_finding",
786	            "demoted_findings",
787	            "class_added",
788	            "class_corrected",
789	        ):
790	            out[k] += res[k]
791	        out["promoted"] += len(res["promoted"])
792	        out["promotion_failures"] += [
793	            {"rid": rid, **f} for f in res["promotion_failures"]
794	        ]
795	        out["reviewer_findings"] += len(res["findings"])
796	        if res["block_unusable"]:
797	            out["block_unusable"].append(rid)
798	    out["per_class"] = telemetry.per_class(results.values(), classes or {})
799	    return out
