"""ledger-v1 reader, the four row checks, linking, demotion, telemetry and promotion (DESIGN 9.1 to 9.4, DD-2, DD-3,
DD-9, DD-11, DD-12).

    read_ledger(report, assigned)   the `## Ledger` block of a reviewer's final message as rows, with every format
                                    problem counted (DESIGN 9.1)
    Corpora / transcript_results    the four places a `quote_other` may come from (DD-2)
    check_report(report, ...)       reader + checks 1 to 4 (9.2) + linking + demotion + `class` telemetry + promotion
                                    (9.3) for one reviewer; returns the checked text (the raw report is never edited)
                                    and every count
    summarise(results)              the per-run check.json of DESIGN 9.4 from the per-reviewer results
    carries_cb3(...)                the CB-3 sentence rule

Findings parsing comes only from scaffold/fnd.py; the telemetry keys and the per-class tables are in scaffold/telemetry.py.

Gaps in DESIGN 9.3 and 9.4 resolved by Task 25 (each is a choice the design leaves open; every one is covered by a test):
  P1  Promotion id. `P<item>`; when that id is already in the block the one suffix `-2` is tried (`PS3-2`; a plain
      digit would make `PS3` + `2` collide with the promoted line of an item `S32`), and a second collision is a
      duplicate id, so `_check_finding` rejects it and the row is a promotion failure. A reviewer has at most one
      row per item (`dup_line`), so a second collision means the reviewer used both ids itself.
  P2  A promoted line is checked with `fnd._check_finding` first and its message is the logged reason. Then two
      conditions the design states elsewhere are added to the same list of failures: the row broke a ledger limit
      (9.1 item 5: "cannot be promoted") and the `problem` is empty (the check never writes a claim of its own, so an
      empty claim is not promoted). An empty `quote_plan` is refused by `_check_finding` itself (anchor minimum).
      A row of an item with no `class` in items.json, or of a class with no card, is also a failure (no category).
      Every failure is logged `{item, id, reason}`; none is silent.
  P3  Promotion asks for no support: the design (9.3) gives the PROBLEM verdict and "no linked findings line" as the
      only conditions. A promoted anchor is the row's `quote_plan` as written, found in the candidate or not.
  P4  "Linked" for promotion means the finding links to the row by probe or by quote, whether or not the row is
      OK, and whether or not the finding line itself is a valid findings line. A broken row (a format error line) is
      not in `rows`, so it is never promoted.
  P5  Telemetry: `class` is written on every linked line whose item has a class in items.json (added when missing,
      corrected when different), also on an OK-row line and on a line that stays blocking. The reviewer's `probe` is
      kept as written and none is added to a quote-linked line. A line is rewritten (`json.dumps`, the line ending
      kept) only when `blocking` or `class` changes; an untouched line keeps its bytes. Corrections are counted in
      `class_corrected`, additions in `class_added` (DESIGN 9.4 has no field for them; they are extra keys of check.json).
  P6  The unusable block: nothing is promoted and no line is touched (G10); `block_unusable` carries the reason in the
      per-reviewer result and the reviewer id in check.json.
  P7  check.json extras beyond the DESIGN 9.4 fields: `reviewer_findings` (the findings lines read, so promoted ones are
      counted apart), `demoted_findings`, `class_added`, `class_corrected`, `per_class` and `no_report` (a reviewer
      with no report file). `missing_line` lists only reviewers whose ledger was read; a `ledger_missing` reviewer is
      under `ledger_missing` alone.

Gaps in DESIGN 9 resolved here (each is a choice the design leaves open; every one is covered by a test):
  G1  `corpus` is the FIRST match in the order of DD-2: source, candidate, sheet, transcript. A quote that is also in
      the transcript only because the reviewer read the candidate (nearly every run) is therefore `candidate`, not
      `transcript`, so a row whose two quotes are the same plan text cannot pass as a "search result". Consequence:
      a `sheet` or `transcript` match is never in the candidate, so it always differs from the plan quote and
      `search_supported` implies `quotes_supported`; the flag is kept because 9.2 check 4 defines it.
  G2  Sheet corpus (9.2 check 3, "a printed tool line of this item"): the evidence `text` of the row's item, and the
      same entry in its printed form (`plan line 85: <text>`, `<path>:12: <text>`; render.py's form).
  G3  Transcript corpus: the string `content` of every `tool_result` block of every `user` event (a list of `text`
      parts is joined per part). One block is one corpus entry: a quote cannot span two tool results. Nothing
      from `assistant` events is read here. Real files: results/transcript-shapes.md.
  G4  Where the ledger is looked for (9.1 items 1 and 2). `findings_heading_missing` (no `## Findings block`, so no
      span), `ledger_heading_missing`, `ledger_after_findings` (every `## Ledger` heading is below the findings
      heading), `heading_between` (another heading, outside code fences, sits between the two), `no_block`,
      `two_blocks` (counted over the whole report, so a stray block before the heading also counts), `unclosed`
      (the fence never closes, or it swallows the findings heading) and `block_outside_span`. Each is
      `ledger_missing` and leaves no rows. The last `## Ledger` heading above the findings heading is the one used.
  G5  A line that is a format error but names an assigned item (`"item": "S2"` is read from the object, or from the
      text by a regular expression when the JSON is broken) makes that item `broken`, unless a good row for it
      exists. A finding linked to a broken row gets the cause `row_missing`. An item with no line at all is in
      `missing_line` and is NOT a broken row; a finding whose probe names it is not linked to anything (there is no
      row) unless its anchor contains another row's `quote_plan`.
  G6  Quote linking needs a `quote_plan` of at least 12 flattened characters (the schema floor), so a three-letter
      quote cannot link every finding.
  G7  A finding that would be demoted for more than one cause counts every cause that holds in `demoted`, and once
      in `demoted_findings`. `format_induced` is true only when every cause is format-induced: `row_missing`, or
      `row_unsupported` where `problem` and both quotes are present and a quote test failed.
  G8  A linked finding whose row is `OK` is left alone whatever its blocking flag (DESIGN 9.3, "left alone"); it is
      counted as `ok_but_finding` whether or not it is blocking.
  G9  `CHECK_SCOPE=all` (never used in an arm): an unlinked blocking finding is held to the same rule with its own
      `anchor` and `anchor2` as the two quotes: `anchor` must be in the candidate, `anchor2` must be in one of the
      four corpora (the sheet corpus is then every item's tool lines), and the two must differ, or `anchor2` is a
      sheet or transcript match. Causes are `row_unsupported` and `no_cb3`.
  G10 When the findings block is unusable (missing, unclosed or duplicated; DESIGN 9.3 "Block repair is out of scope")
      the text comes back unchanged and `block_unusable` names the reason; rows are still read and checked.
  G11 `CB-3` window: the sentence counts when it lies within 12 lines above or below a line that holds the finding
      id as a whole word, in the report text above the `## Findings block` heading. Lines are joined and flattened
      first, so a sentence wrapped over two lines still counts.
  Not resolved (the design gives no number): `quote_other` has no minimum length, so a very short second quote
  passes check 3 if it occurs anywhere in a corpus.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence
from pathlib import Path

from scaffold import cards as cards_mod
from scaffold import fnd, telemetry

HEAD_LEDGER = re.compile(r"^#{1,6}\s+Ledger\s*$", re.M | re.I)
_HEADING_LINE = re.compile(r"^#{1,6}\s+\S")
_FENCE_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s{0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})\s*([^`\s]*)\s*$")
_ITEM_TEXT = re.compile(r'"item"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"')

CB3_SENTENCE = "An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds"
VERDICTS = ("OK", "PROBLEM", "UNSURE")
CAUSES = ("row_unsupported", "row_unsure", "no_cb3", "row_missing")
SCOPES = ("linked", "all")
CORPORA = ("source", "candidate", "sheet", "transcript")
QUOTE_PLAN_MIN = 12
QUOTE_PLAN_MAX = 200
PROBLEM_MAX = 300
RAN_MAX_WORDS = 15
CB3_WINDOW = 12
_TEXT_KEYS = ("quote_plan", "quote_other", "problem", "ran")
_CB3_FLAT = fnd.flat(CB3_SENTENCE).lower()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- positions and fences


def _line_of(text: str, pos: int) -> int:
    """1-based line number of character offset pos."""
    return text.count("\n", 0, pos) + 1


def _fenced(report: str, info: str) -> list[tuple[int, list[tuple[int, str]], bool]]:
    """Every fenced block of the whole report with this info string, like fnd._blocks_after but not tied to a heading.

    A one-line heading is put in front of the text so the scan starts at the first real line; the numbers it returns
    are shifted back, so they are lines of `report`.
    """
    _, blocks = fnd._blocks_after("#\n" + report, re.compile(r"^#\n", re.M), info)
    return [
        (s - 1, [(n - 1, t) for n, t in body], closed) for s, body, closed in blocks
    ]


def _heading_between(lines: list[str], first: int, last: int) -> bool:
    """True when a heading line outside a code fence sits on a line strictly between `first` and `last` (1-based)."""
    marker: str | None = None
    for n in range(first + 1, last):
        line = lines[n - 1]
        fm = _FENCE_LINE.match(line)
        if marker is None:
            if fm:
                marker = fm.group(1)
            elif _HEADING_LINE.match(line):
                return True
        elif (
            fm
            and not fm.group(2)
            and fm.group(1)[0] == marker[0]
            and len(fm.group(1)) >= len(marker)
        ):
            marker = None
    return False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 9.1 the reader


def _recover_item(raw: str, obj: object) -> str | None:
    if isinstance(obj, dict) and isinstance(obj.get("item"), str):
        return obj["item"].strip() or None
    m = _ITEM_TEXT.search(raw)
    return m.group(1).strip() if m else None


def read_ledger(report: str, assigned: Sequence[str]) -> dict:
    """The ledger of a final message (DESIGN 9.1) as a dict.

    {"ledger_missing": bool, "reason": str | None, "rows": [row], "format_errors": [{line, msg}],
     "normalised_verdict": n, "dup_line": [{line, item}], "unknown_item": [{line, item}],
     "broken_items": [item], "missing_line": [item]}

    A row is {item, verdict, quote_plan, quote_other, problem, ran, line, limits_violated: [name]}. The verdict is
    upper-cased and trimmed. Rows come back in the order of the lines. When `ledger_missing` is true `rows` is empty and
    `missing_line` holds every assigned item.
    """
    assigned = list(assigned)
    res: dict = {
        "ledger_missing": True,
        "reason": None,
        "rows": [],
        "format_errors": [],
        "normalised_verdict": 0,
        "dup_line": [],
        "unknown_item": [],
        "broken_items": [],
        "missing_line": list(assigned),
    }
    fm = fnd._HEAD_FINDINGS.search(report)
    if not fm:
        res["reason"] = "findings_heading_missing"
        return res
    f_line = _line_of(report, fm.start())
    heads = [_line_of(report, m.start()) for m in HEAD_LEDGER.finditer(report)]
    above = [h for h in heads if h < f_line]
    if not above:
        res["reason"] = "ledger_after_findings" if heads else "ledger_heading_missing"
        return res
    l_line = above[-1]
    if _heading_between(report.splitlines(), l_line, f_line):
        res["reason"] = "heading_between"
        return res
    blocks = _fenced(report, "ledger-v1")
    if not blocks:
        res["reason"] = "no_block"
        return res
    if len(blocks) > 1:
        res["reason"] = "two_blocks"
        return res
    start, body, closed = blocks[0]
    if not l_line < start < f_line:
        res["reason"] = "block_outside_span"
        return res
    if not closed or (body and body[-1][0] >= f_line):
        res["reason"] = "unclosed"
        return res
    res["ledger_missing"] = False

    by_item: dict[str, dict] = {}
    broken: dict[str, int] = {}

    def error(lineno: int, msg: str, item: str | None) -> None:
        res["format_errors"].append({"line": lineno, "msg": msg})
        if item and item in assigned:
            broken.setdefault(item, lineno)

    for lineno, raw in body:
        if not raw.strip():
            continue
        try:
            obj = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            error(lineno, f"not valid JSON: {exc.msg}", _recover_item(raw, None))
            continue
        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
            error(lineno, "a line must be a JSON object", None)
            continue
        item, verdict = obj.get("item"), obj.get("verdict")
        known = _recover_item(raw, obj)
        if not isinstance(item, str) or not item.strip():
            error(lineno, "item is missing or not a string", known)
            continue
        if not isinstance(verdict, str):
            error(lineno, "verdict is missing or not a string", known)
            continue
        canon = verdict.strip().upper()
        if canon not in VERDICTS:
            error(lineno, "verdict must be OK, PROBLEM or UNSURE", known)
            continue
        values = {k: ("" if obj.get(k) is None else obj[k]) for k in _TEXT_KEYS}
        bad = [k for k, v in values.items() if not isinstance(v, str)]
        if bad:
            error(lineno, f"{', '.join(bad)} must be a string", known)
            continue
        if canon != verdict:
            res["normalised_verdict"] += 1
        item = item.strip()
        if item not in assigned:
            res["unknown_item"].append({"line": lineno, "item": item})
            continue
        if item in by_item:
            res["dup_line"].append({"line": lineno, "item": item})
            continue
        limits = []
        qp = fnd.flat(values["quote_plan"])
        if qp and not QUOTE_PLAN_MIN <= len(qp) <= QUOTE_PLAN_MAX:
            limits.append("quote_plan")
        if len(fnd.flat(values["problem"])) > PROBLEM_MAX:
            limits.append("problem")
        if len(values["ran"].split()) > RAN_MAX_WORDS:
            limits.append("ran")
        by_item[item] = {
            "item": item,
            "verdict": canon,
            **values,
            "line": lineno,
            "limits_violated": limits,
        }
        res["rows"].append(by_item[item])
    res["broken_items"] = [i for i in assigned if i in broken and i not in by_item]
    res["missing_line"] = [
        i for i in assigned if i not in by_item and i not in res["broken_items"]
    ]
    return res


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 9.2 corpora and the four checks


def transcript_results(events: object) -> list[str]:
    """The tool results of a run transcript (the parsed `*.attempt1.json`): one string per `tool_result` block (G3)."""
    out: list[str] = []
    if not isinstance(events, list):
        return out
    for ev in events:
        if not isinstance(ev, dict) or ev.get("type") != "user":
            continue
        message = ev.get("message")
        content = message.get("content") if isinstance(message, dict) else None
        if not isinstance(content, list):
            continue
        for block in content:
            if not isinstance(block, dict) or block.get("type") != "tool_result":
                continue
            c = block.get("content")
            if isinstance(c, str):
                out.append(c)
            elif isinstance(c, list):
                out += [
                    p["text"]
                    for p in c
                    if isinstance(p, dict)
                    and p.get("type") == "text"
                    and isinstance(p.get("text"), str)
                ]
    return out


def read_transcript(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
    """transcript_results of the JSON file at path."""
    return transcript_results(json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))


def _printed_lines(item: dict) -> list[str]:
    """The tool lines of an item as the reader of the sheet sees them (G2): the entry text, and its printed form."""
    out = []
    for e in item.get("evidence") or []:
        text = e.get("text", "")
        out.append(text)
        path, line = e.get("path"), e.get("line")
        if line and path in ("plan", "source"):
            out.append(f"{path} line {line}: {text}")
        elif line and path:
            out.append(f"{path}:{line}: {text}")
    return out


class Corpora:
    """The four places a `quote_other` may come from (DD-2): `source`, `candidate`, `sheet`, `transcript`.

    `items` are the item dicts of items.json (`item_id`, `evidence`); `transcript` is a list of tool-result strings.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        candidate: str,
        source: str | None = None,
        items: Iterable[dict] = (),
        transcript: Iterable[str] = (),
    ):
        self.candidate = candidate
        self.source = source
        self._sheet = {
            it["item_id"]: [fnd.flat(t) for t in _printed_lines(it)] for it in items
        }
        self._transcript = [fnd.flat(t) for t in transcript]

    def in_candidate(self, quote: str) -> bool:
        return bool(fnd.locate(self.candidate, quote))

    def find(self, quote: str, item: str | None = None) -> str | None:
        """The first corpus, in the order of DD-2, that holds the flattened quote (G1); None when none does.

        The sheet corpus is the tool lines of `item`, or of every item when `item` is None.
        """
        q = fnd.flat(quote)
        if not q:
            return None
        if self.source is not None and fnd.locate(self.source, q):
            return "source"
        if fnd.locate(self.candidate, q):
            return "candidate"
        pools = (
            self._sheet.get(item, [])
            if item is not None
            else [t for v in self._sheet.values() for t in v]
        )
        if any(q in t for t in pools):
            return "sheet"
        if any(q in t for t in self._transcript):
            return "transcript"
        return None


def _support(plan_ok: bool, other_ok: bool, corpus: str | None, same: bool) -> dict:
    quotes = plan_ok and other_ok and not same
    search = plan_ok and other_ok and corpus in ("sheet", "transcript")
    return {
        "quotes_supported": quotes,
        "search_supported": search,
        "supported": quotes or search,
    }


def check_row(row: dict, corpora: Corpora) -> dict:
    """Checks 2 to 4 of DESIGN 9.2 for one row: the row plus quote_plan_ok, quote_other_ok, corpus and the support flags."""
    plan_ok = bool(row["quote_plan"].strip()) and corpora.in_candidate(
        row["quote_plan"]
    )
    corpus = corpora.find(row["quote_other"], row["item"])
    same = fnd.flat(row["quote_plan"]) == fnd.flat(row["quote_other"])
    return {
        **row,
        "quote_plan_ok": plan_ok,
        "quote_other_ok": corpus is not None,
        "corpus": corpus,
        **_support(plan_ok, corpus is not None, corpus, same),
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 9.3 the CB-3 sentence, linking, demotion


def carries_cb3(finding: dict, lines_above: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
    """True when the finding carries the CB-3 sentence (DESIGN 9.3, G11).

    `lines_above` are the report lines above the `## Findings block` heading. The comparison is flattened and
    case-insensitive.
    """
    claim = finding.get("claim")
    if isinstance(claim, str) and _CB3_FLAT in fnd.flat(claim).lower():
        return True
    fid = finding.get("id")
    if not isinstance(fid, str):
        return False
    mention = re.compile(
        rf"(?<![A-Za-z0-9._-]){re.escape(fid)}(?![A-Za-z0-9_-]|\.[A-Za-z0-9])"
    )
    for i, line in enumerate(lines_above):
        if mention.search(line):
            window = " ".join(lines_above[max(0, i - CB3_WINDOW) : i + CB3_WINDOW + 1])
            if _CB3_FLAT in fnd.flat(window).lower():
                return True
    return False


def findings_block_status(report: str) -> tuple[str | None, tuple | None]:
    """(reason the block is unusable or None, the block). The block is (fence line, [(line, text)], closed)."""
    found, blocks = fnd._blocks_after(report, fnd._HEAD_FINDINGS, "findings-v1")
    if not found:
        return "findings_heading_missing", None
    if not blocks:
        return "no_findings_block", None
    if len(blocks) > 1:
        return "findings_block_duplicated", None
    if not blocks[0][2]:
        return "findings_block_unclosed", None
    return None, blocks[0]


def scope_from(scope: str | None = None) -> str:
    """`scope`, else the environment variable CHECK_SCOPE, else `linked` (DD-3)."""
    value = scope if scope is not None else (os.environ.get("CHECK_SCOPE") or "linked")
    if value not in SCOPES:
        raise ValueError(f"CHECK_SCOPE must be one of {SCOPES}, not {value!r}")
    return value


def _link(finding: dict, assigned: list[str], rows: dict, broken: list[str], ordered):
    """(row or None, how, probe_unknown). `how` is "probe", "quote" or None; a broken row is {"item", "broken": True}."""
    probe = finding.get("probe")
    unknown = False
    if isinstance(probe, str) and probe.strip():
        p = probe.strip()
        if p not in assigned:
            unknown = True
        elif p in rows:
            return rows[p], "probe", False
        elif p in broken:
            return {"item": p, "broken": True}, "probe", False
    anchor = (
        fnd.flat(finding["anchor"]) if isinstance(finding.get("anchor"), str) else ""
    )
    for row in ordered:
        qp = fnd.flat(row["quote_plan"])
        if len(qp) >= QUOTE_PLAN_MIN and qp in anchor:
            return row, "quote", unknown
    return None, None, unknown


def _own_quotes(finding: dict, corpora: Corpora) -> dict:
    """Support of an unlinked finding under CHECK_SCOPE=all (G9): its anchor and anchor2 are the two quotes."""
    anchor, anchor2 = finding.get("anchor"), finding.get("anchor2")
    plan_ok = isinstance(anchor, str) and corpora.in_candidate(anchor)
    corpus = corpora.find(anchor2) if isinstance(anchor2, str) else None
    same = fnd.flat(anchor or "") == fnd.flat(anchor2 or "")
    return _support(plan_ok, corpus is not None, corpus, same)


def _row_causes(row: dict) -> tuple[list[str], bool]:
    """(causes, format_induced) for a linked, blocking finding, apart from no_cb3."""
    if row.get("broken"):
        return ["row_missing"], True
    if row["verdict"] == "UNSURE":
        return ["row_unsure"], False
    if row["verdict"] == "PROBLEM" and not row["supported"]:
        fmt = bool(
            row["problem"].strip()
            and row["quote_plan"].strip()
            and row["quote_other"].strip()
            and not (row["quote_plan_ok"] and row["quote_other_ok"])
        )
        return ["row_unsupported"], fmt
    return [], False


def check_report(
    report: str,
    *,
    assigned: Sequence[str],
    candidate: str,
    source: str | None = None,
    items: Iterable[dict] = (),
    transcript: Iterable[str] = (),
    scope: str | None = None,
    cards: dict[str, dict] | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """One reviewer's report through the reader, checks 1 to 4, linking, demotion, telemetry and promotion.

    `items` are the item dicts of items.json (`item_id`, `class`, `evidence`); the class of an item is where the
    `class` key and the promotion category come from (the card of the class, `cards`, default cards/).

    Returns {"scope", "ledger": <read_ledger result, rows checked>, "block_unusable": reason | None,
    "findings": [per finding: id, line, probe, row_item, link, class, class_change, blocking, demoted, causes,
    format_induced, ok_but_finding], "probe_unknown": n, "ok_but_finding": n, "demoted": {cause: n},
    "demoted_findings": n, "format_induced_demotions": n, "class_added": n, "class_corrected": n,
    "promoted": [{id, item, class, line}], "promotion_failures": [{item, id, reason}], "text": the checked report}.
    `text` is `report` with the demotions, the `class` keys and the promoted lines written; it is `report` itself
    when the block is unusable or nothing changes. The raw report is never edited.
    """
    scope = scope_from(scope)
    assigned = list(assigned)
    items = list(items)
    classes = {it["item_id"]: it["class"] for it in items if it.get("class")}
    corpora = Corpora(candidate, source, items, list(transcript))
    ledger = read_ledger(report, assigned)
    ledger["rows"] = [check_row(r, corpora) for r in ledger["rows"]]
    rows = {r["item"]: r for r in ledger["rows"]}
    out = {
        "scope": scope,
        "ledger": ledger,
        "block_unusable": None,
        "findings": [],
        "probe_unknown": 0,
        "ok_but_finding": 0,
        "demoted": dict.fromkeys(CAUSES, 0),
        "demoted_findings": 0,
        "format_induced_demotions": 0,
        "class_added": 0,
        "class_corrected": 0,
        "promoted": [],
        "promotion_failures": [],
        "text": report,
    }
    reason, block = findings_block_status(report)
    if reason:
        out["block_unusable"] = reason
        return out
    lines = report.splitlines(keepends=True)
    f_line = _line_of(report, fnd._HEAD_FINDINGS.search(report).start())
    above = [ln.rstrip("\r\n") for ln in lines[: f_line - 1]]
    changed = False
    for lineno, raw in block[1]:
        try:
            obj = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if (
            not isinstance(obj, dict)
            or "prior" in obj
            or not isinstance(obj.get("id"), str)
        ):
            continue
        row, how, unknown = _link(
            obj, assigned, rows, ledger["broken_items"], ledger["rows"]
        )
        out["probe_unknown"] += unknown
        item_class = classes.get(row["item"]) if row else None
        rec = {
            "id": obj["id"],
            "line": lineno,
            "probe": obj.get("probe"),
            "row_item": row["item"] if row else None,
            "link": how,
            "class": item_class,
            "class_change": None,
            "blocking": obj.get("blocking") is True,
            "demoted": False,
            "causes": [],
            "format_induced": False,
            "ok_but_finding": False,
        }
        out["findings"].append(rec)
        rewrite = False
        state = telemetry.fill_class(obj, item_class)  # DD-12 (P5)
        if state:
            rec["class_change"] = state
            out[f"class_{state}"] += 1
            rewrite = True
        if row is not None and not row.get("broken") and row["verdict"] == "OK":
            out["ok_but_finding"] += 1
            rec["ok_but_finding"] = True
        elif rec["blocking"] and (row is not None or scope == "all"):
            if row is not None:
                causes, fmt = _row_causes(row)
            else:
                causes, fmt = (
                    (
                        []
                        if _own_quotes(obj, corpora)["supported"]
                        else ["row_unsupported"]
                    ),
                    False,
                )
            if not carries_cb3(obj, above):
                causes.append("no_cb3")
            if causes:
                rec.update(
                    demoted=True,
                    causes=causes,
                    format_induced=fmt and "no_cb3" not in causes,
                )
                for c in causes:
                    out["demoted"][c] += 1
                out["demoted_findings"] += 1
                out["format_induced_demotions"] += rec["format_induced"]
                obj["blocking"] = False
                rewrite = True
        if rewrite:
            lines[lineno - 1] = (
                json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False) + lines[lineno - 1][len(raw) :]
            )
            changed = True
    linked = {rec["row_item"] for rec in out["findings"] if rec["link"]}
    todo = [
        r
        for r in ledger["rows"]
        if r["verdict"] == "PROBLEM" and r["item"] not in linked
    ]
    if todo:
        changed |= _promote(todo, block, lines, classes, cards, out)
    if changed:
        out["text"] = "".join(lines)
    return out


def _promotion_line(
    row: dict, item_class: str | None, cards: dict | None, seen: set[str]
) -> tuple[dict | None, str, str | None]:
    """(the promoted line or None, its id, the reason it was refused or None) for one PROBLEM row (DESIGN 9.3, P1, P2)."""
    base = f"P{row['item']}"
    pid = base if base not in seen else f"{base}-2"
    if not item_class:
        return (
            None,
            pid,
            "the item has no class in items.json: no category to promote under",
        )
    try:
        category = cards_mod.promote_category(item_class, cards)
    except KeyError:
        return None, pid, f"no card for class {item_class}"
    line = {
        "id": pid,
        "severity": "MINOR",
        "blocking": False,
        "category": category,
        "anchor": row["quote_plan"],
        "refs": [],
        "claim": row["problem"],
        **telemetry.promoted_keys(row["item"], item_class),
    }
    err = fnd._check_finding(line, seen)
    if err is None and not row["problem"].strip():
        err = "problem is empty: the check writes no claim of its own"
    if err is None and row["limits_violated"]:
        err = "the row breaks a ledger limit: " + ", ".join(row["limits_violated"])
    return (None if err else line), pid, err


def _promote(
    todo: list[dict],
    block: tuple,
    lines: list[str],
    classes: dict[str, str],
    cards: dict | None,
    out: dict,
) -> bool:
    """Insert one MINOR, non-blocking line per row of `todo` as the last lines inside the one findings block (9.3).

    `lines` (the report with line endings) is edited in place. A refused row goes to out["promotion_failures"] and is
    skipped; an inserted one to out["promoted"]. True when a line was inserted.
    """
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for _, raw in block[1]:
        try:
            obj = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if (
            isinstance(obj, dict)
            and "prior" not in obj
            and isinstance(obj.get("id"), str)
        ):
            seen.add(obj["id"])
    close = block[0] + len(
        block[1]
    )  # 0-based index of the closing fence: opener line n is index n-1
    eol = "\r\n" if lines[close - 1].endswith("\r\n") else "\n"
    new: list[str] = []
    for row in todo:
        item_class = classes.get(row["item"])
        line, pid, err = _promotion_line(row, item_class, cards, seen)
        if err:
            out["promotion_failures"].append(
                {"item": row["item"], "id": pid, "reason": err}
            )
            continue
        seen.add(pid)
        new.append(json.dumps(line, ensure_ascii=False) + eol)
        out["promoted"].append(
            {
                "id": pid,
                "item": row["item"],
                "class": item_class,
                "line": close + 1 + len(new) - 1,
            }
        )
    lines[close:close] = new
    return bool(new)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 9.4 the per-run check.json


def summarise(
    results: dict[str, dict],
    classes: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    no_report: Sequence[str] = (),
) -> dict:
    """check.json of DESIGN 9.4 from {reviewer id: check_report result}, with the extras of P7.

    Reviewer findings and promoted findings are counted apart: `reviewer_findings` is the findings lines the
    reviewers wrote, `promoted` the lines the check inserted. `classes` is {item id: class} for the per-class tables.
    """
    out: dict = {
        "ledger_missing": [],
        "format_errors": 0,
        "normalised_verdict": 0,
        "dup_line": 0,
        "unknown_item": 0,
        "probe_unknown": 0,
        "missing_line": {},
        "rows": dict.fromkeys(VERDICTS, 0),
        "demoted": dict.fromkeys(CAUSES, 0),
        "format_induced_demotions": 0,
        "promoted": 0,
        "promotion_failures": [],
        "ok_but_finding": 0,
        "block_unusable": [],
        "reviewer_findings": 0,
        "demoted_findings": 0,
        "class_added": 0,
        "class_corrected": 0,
        "per_class": {},
        "no_report": list(no_report),
    }
    for rid, res in results.items():
        led = res["ledger"]
        if led["ledger_missing"]:
            out["ledger_missing"].append(rid)
        elif led["missing_line"]:
            out["missing_line"][rid] = list(led["missing_line"])
        out["format_errors"] += len(led["format_errors"])
        out["normalised_verdict"] += led["normalised_verdict"]
        out["dup_line"] += len(led["dup_line"])
        out["unknown_item"] += len(led["unknown_item"])
        for r in led["rows"]:
            out["rows"][r["verdict"]] += 1
        for c in CAUSES:
            out["demoted"][c] += res["demoted"][c]
        for k in (
            "probe_unknown",
            "format_induced_demotions",
            "ok_but_finding",
            "demoted_findings",
            "class_added",
            "class_corrected",
        ):
            out[k] += res[k]
        out["promoted"] += len(res["promoted"])
        out["promotion_failures"] += [
            {"rid": rid, **f} for f in res["promotion_failures"]
        ]
        out["reviewer_findings"] += len(res["findings"])
        if res["block_unusable"]:
            out["block_unusable"].append(rid)
    out["per_class"] = telemetry.per_class(results.values(), classes or {})
    return out

# Owner decisions for the Sweep Sheet validation (DESIGN.md section 15.1)

## 1. G0 selection-recall floor: 0.45, pooled (confirmed by the owner, 2026-11-15)

- Pre-register it with this wording: "an estimate, not a validated figure". Report the measured selection recall with its range whatever the result.
- It is a go/no-go gate for spending model runs, not a claim that the sheet helps. A pass says the sheet can contain the right item; whether reviewers act on it is measured separately.
- Basis (recomputed 2026-11-15 from the ten rows of the coverage table in `.dev/brainstorms/20261113-223124-panel-process-redesign/merged-requirements.md`, section 3.1(d)): mean of the lower ends of the selection estimates 0.480 (0.506 without the experimental C3 row); mean of the upper ends 0.740; mid-point 0.610. All inputs are unmeasured estimates, so the floor is not independent of the design it tests.
- Chance of passing, assuming 20 to 40 hold-out issues (binomial calculation, not measured): true recall 0.25: 0 to 4%; 0.35: 12 to 24%; 0.48: 63 to 70%; 0.61: 95 to 99%; 0.74: 100%.
- Do not raise it: at 0.50 the mid-point case passes only about 90% of the time.
- Not done yet: the value is not written into `config/prereg.json`. That happens at the freeze (`analysis/analyze.py prereg`), which is plan step 14 and has not been run.

## 2. to 4. Adopted under the owner's order of 2026-11-15 ("adversarially debate all 3 sets of defaults; if they pass, proceed with them; if not, refactor and then proceed")

Debates: three advocates each (Haiku-alias, Sonnet, Sonnet) plus a fault-finder; no Opus. Opus is not in any session's model usage. The Haiku alias resolved on this gateway to `gpt-6.1-sol` for at least some advocate turns (the session transcripts record that model name), so the "Haiku" advocate was not Claude Haiku. Debate depth standard; the orchestrator and merge were done by the Sonnet session, scoring condensed, so the verdicts are not an independent score. After the debates the sweep-sheet tests pass again (749 passed, 4 deselected) with the edits in place.

| # | Default | Verdict | Adopted value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Per-class act bands | FAIL on the numbers-only default (no measure, no comparison rule, no consequence), refactored | The eight numbers unchanged (C1 0.10-0.40, C2 0.20-0.45, C3 0.03-0.15, C4 0.50-0.75, C5 0.35-0.60, C6 0.05-0.30, C7 0.15-0.35, C8 0.40-0.65) with the registration text of `DESIGN.md` section 15.1a: the measure, a 95% Wilson rule (under 10 item-runs "not assessable"), a report-only consequence, and a may-not list. See `results/debate/1-act-bands/VERDICT.md`. |
| 3 | CB-2 | PASS | Leave `briefs/cb2.txt` verbatim in every arm; count the `## Ledger` headings in Z0 and K. No file changed. See `results/debate/2-cb2-verbatim/VERDICT.md` (note: "owner decision if above 0" has no content yet). |
| 4 | K-arm lead-in | PASS | Approve `briefs/k-lead.txt` as drafted. No file changed. See `results/debate/3-k-lead/VERDICT.md`. |

Limits recorded by the debates: the act-band numbers are unmeasured planning values; nothing computes the new act-band measure or flag yet (`analysis/analyze.py`, `prereg()` and the tests were not edited, so the rule is applied by hand until a follow-up adds code and tests); the act-band text is not in `config/prereg.json` yet (that is plan step 14, the freeze, which has not been run); the BD-3 fix and probe-driven additions were not re-debated.

Commit id: none yet (nothing committed).

- The freeze go (plan step 14), the document list (D1), and sharing of one control (D2): see `20261114-collab-process/PROCESS.md` section 8.

"""The one import point for superclaude.cli.review.findings (DESIGN 2.3).

Everything in scaffold/ and sweep/ gets the real parser from here. `_check_finding` and `_blocks_after` are
private in the source; tests/test_fnd_contract.py pins their names and signatures, so a rename or change shows
up in that one test and this file is the only one to edit.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from superclaude.cli.review.findings import (  # noqa: F401  (re-exports)
    _HEAD_FINDINGS,
    CATEGORIES,
    _blocks_after,
    _check_finding,
    flat,
    locate,
    parse_block,
    same_defect,
)


def lenient_lines(report: str) -> list[str]:
    """The raw lines of the findings block (the last findings-v1 fence, like parse_block), blank lines dropped.

    Lines are returned as written, valid JSON or not, so a caller can repair or count the bad ones.
    No heading or no findings-v1 fence gives []. An unclosed fence still gives the lines read before the end.
    """
    _, blocks = _blocks_after(report, _HEAD_FINDINGS, "findings-v1")
    if not blocks:
        return []
    return [raw for _, raw in blocks[-1][1] if raw.strip()]

441	Consequences, each tested: an empty-sheet SS brief is byte-equal to the Z0 brief of the same document (REQ-23, compared by sha256); CB-1 is absent and `no_source` is logged when there is no source file (REQ-01); no part contains the string `src/superclaude/` (REQ-09); the quoted parts equal the quoted blocks of `MR` (REQ-05); the first line `/sc:spec-panel @<candidate> --mode critique` of `RR` line 13 is kept in every arm.
442	
443	The text of the ledger rule and the sheet block is draft wording that has not been run on any model (`MR`, "Not checked and unverified"). The compliance spike (section 14.2) is the first run of it.
444	
445	### 8.2 What the reviewer is told, in one picture
446	
447	The reviewer's final message must look like this. The headings and info strings are exactly those of `MR` 3.0.4. Everything before `## Ledger` is free text.
448	
449	````
450	<report text, including the grading sentences>
451	
452	## Ledger
453	
454	```ledger-v1
455	{"item":"S3","verdict":"PROBLEM","quote_plan":"<12-200 chars from the plan>","quote_other":"<exact text>","problem":"<one sentence, at most 300 chars>","ran":"<at most 15 words>"}
456	{"item":"S7","verdict":"OK","quote_plan":"","quote_other":"","problem":"","ran":"compared both scopes"}
457	```
458	
459	## Findings block
460	
461	```findings-v1
462	{"id":"F1","severity":"MAJOR","blocking":false,"category":"other","anchor":"<12-200 chars>","refs":[],"claim":"<one sentence>","probe":"S3"}
463	```
464	
465	verdict: FAIL
466	````
467	
468	## 9. Ledger, checks and promotion (`scaffold/ledgerv1.py`, `sweep/cli.py check`)
469	
470	### 9.1 Reading the final message
471	
472	`RR` keeps only the final result message as the report (`RR` line 50), and checks only that a line starts with the `findings-v1` fence opener (`RR` line 57). The check therefore reads the report file `reviews/<rid>.md` with a real parser:
473	
474	1. Find the heading `## Ledger` (regex `^#{1,6}\s+Ledger\s*$`, case-insensitive) and the heading `## Findings block` (the same regex `FND` uses). The ledger heading must come first and no other heading may sit between them ("directly above", REQ-13).
475	2. In the text between the two headings, find fenced blocks with info string `ledger-v1` (`FND._blocks_after`, through the adapter). Zero blocks, two blocks, an unclosed block or a block outside that span means `ledger_missing` for this reviewer.
476	3. Parse each non-empty line as JSON. A line that is not valid JSON, is not an object, or lacks `item` or `verdict` is a **format error** and is counted (`format_errors`, with the line number). It is never skipped silently.
477	4. Accepted leniency, counted separately (`normalised_verdict`): the verdict is read case-insensitively and trimmed.
478	5. Limits: `quote_plan` is empty or 12 to 200 flattened characters; `problem` at most 300; `ran` at most 15 words; `item` must be one of the items assigned to this reviewer, otherwise `unknown_item`. A row that breaks a limit is kept for coverage and flagged `limits_violated`; it cannot be promoted.
479	6. A second line for the same item is `dup_line`; the first wins.
480	
481	Earlier assistant messages in the transcript are read for the `transcript` corpus (DD-2) and for diagnosis only. They never feed promotion and never change `ledger_missing` (`MR` 3.0.4).
482	
483	### 9.2 Checks (per reviewer, per row)
484	
485	| # | Check | Result recorded |
486	|---|---|---|
487	| 1 | Every item assigned to the reviewer has a ledger line | `missing_line: [S5, ...]`. No re-ask (time). |
488	| 2 | `quote_plan` is a flattened substring of the candidate (`FND.locate` is non-empty) | `quote_plan_ok` |
489	| 3 | `quote_other` is a flattened substring of the source, the candidate, a printed tool line of this item, or a tool result of the reviewer's own transcript | `quote_other_ok`, `corpus` |
490	| 4 | Row support. `quotes_supported`: `quote_plan_ok` and `quote_other_ok` and the two flattened quotes differ. `search_supported`: `quote_plan_ok` and `quote_other_ok` and `corpus` is `sheet` or `transcript` | `supported = quotes_supported or search_supported` |
491	
492	All substring tests use `FND.flat` and `FND.locate`, so a quote that wraps a plan line still matches (REQ-14).
493	
494	### 9.3 Linking, demotion, promotion
495	
496	**Link.** A findings line is linked to a ledger row when its `probe` equals the row's `item`, or when the row's flattened `quote_plan` lies inside the finding's flattened `anchor` (`MR` 3.0.5, "Linking"). A `probe` that names an item not assigned to this reviewer is `probe_unknown` and does not link.
497	
498	**Demotion** (applies to linked findings only, DD-3). A linked finding with `blocking: true` is set to `blocking: false` (severity stays; a `CRITICAL` or `MAJOR` non-blocking line is valid) when any of these holds. Each cause is counted separately, because format-induced demotions must be reported (INV-007):
499	
500	| Cause | Condition |
501	|---|---|
502	| `row_unsupported` | the linked row is `PROBLEM` and `supported` is false |
503	| `row_unsure` | the linked row is `UNSURE` |
504	| `no_cb3` | the finding does not carry the CB-3 sentence (below) |
505	| `row_missing` | the linked row failed to parse (a format error line) |
506	
507	A linked finding whose row is `OK` is left alone and counted as `ok_but_finding`.
508	
509	**The CB-3 sentence.** The text `An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds` (compared after flattening, case-insensitive) must appear in the finding's `claim`, or in the report text within 12 lines of a line that mentions the finding's id as a whole word, before the findings block.
510	
511	**Promotion** (a `PROBLEM` row with no linked findings line; `UNSURE` and `OK` rows are never promoted). The check never writes a claim of its own:
512	
513	| Field | Value |
514	|---|---|
515	| `id` | `P` + the item id (for example `PS3`); a numeric suffix is added if the id is already used in the block |
516	| `severity`, `blocking` | `MINOR`, `false` |
517	| `category` | the class card's `promote_category` (DD-11) |
518	| `anchor` | the row's `quote_plan` (a row with an empty `quote_plan` is not promoted) |
519	| `claim` | the row's `problem`, copied unchanged |
520	| `refs` | `[]` |
521	| telemetry | `"class": "<C1-C8>"`, `"probe": "<item id>"`, `"src": "ledger"` |
522	
523	The line is built as an object and validated with `_check_finding` (REQ-15) against the ids already in the block; it is inserted as the last line inside the one existing `findings-v1` block, before the closing fence; it is never written as a second block. On any failure the row is logged in `check.json: promotion_failures` and skipped. Promoted findings are counted apart from reviewer findings in every metric.
524	
525	**Telemetry on reviewer lines.** For every linked line the check adds `"class"` (from the item) and keeps the reviewer's `probe`. `FND` does not reject unknown keys (`_check_finding`, lines 90-121, has no key whitelist), and `LED.merge_round` copies only fixed fields into a ledger row (`row` at lines 184-202; members carry only round, reviewer id, finding id and blocking). So the keys never reach `merged-1.md` or `merged/ledger.json`. Telemetry is therefore read from `check/<rid>.checked.md` and joined to the merged ledger through `(reviewer_id, finding id)`. REQ-11 is a test with the real merge.
526	
527	**Block repair is out of scope.** If the `findings-v1` block is missing, unclosed or duplicated, the check changes nothing for that reviewer (it cannot insert a promoted line) and records `block_unusable`. The merge then handles the reviewer as it does today (`LED.merge_round` skips a reviewer with an invalid block for clearing but keeps its parsable lines).
528	
529	### 9.4 Outputs
530	
531	`check/<rid>.ledger.json`: the parsed rows with every check result. `check/<rid>.checked.md`: the report with demotions and promotions applied (the raw `reviews/<rid>.md` is never edited). `check/check.json`:
532	
533	```
534	{ "ledger_missing": [rid, ...], "format_errors": n, "normalised_verdict": n, "dup_line": n, "unknown_item": n,
535	  "probe_unknown": n, "missing_line": {rid: [item, ...]}, "rows": {"OK": n, "PROBLEM": n, "UNSURE": n},
536	  "demoted": {"row_unsupported": n, "row_unsure": n, "no_cb3": n, "row_missing": n},
537	  "format_induced_demotions": n,   // demotions whose row failed only on a quote-match or a parse, not on content
538	  "promoted": n, "promotion_failures": [...], "ok_but_finding": n, "block_unusable": [rid, ...] }
539	```
540	
541	`format_induced_demotions` counts demotions where the row's `problem` text is non-empty and both quotes are present but a quote test failed, or a line failed to parse. It is the number that tells whether the 0.914 squared figure of `MR` 3.0.5 item 4 shows up in practice.
542	
543	### 9.5 Flags
544	
545	| Flag | Meaning | Written to |
546	|---|---|---|
547	| `fallback=true` | the Z0 brief was run because the pre-pass or the render failed | `run.json` |
548	| `no_trigger=true` | the sheet was empty; the brief equals Z0's | `run.json` |
549	| `no_source=true` | no source file; CB-1 and E5 not applied | `run.json` |
550	| `check_skipped=true` | the post-run check raised; demotion and promotion skipped for the whole run and the findings block merged as written | `run.json`, `check/error.log` |
551	| `ledger_missing` | per reviewer, in section 9.1 | `check.json` |
552	
553	## 10. Failure and fallback behaviour

3. Parse each non-empty line as JSON. A line that is not valid JSON, is not an object, or lacks `item` or `verdict` is a **format error** and is counted (`format_errors`, with the line number). It is never skipped silently.
4. Accepted leniency, counted separately (`normalised_verdict`): the verdict is read case-insensitively and trimmed.
5. Limits: `quote_plan` is empty or 12 to 200 flattened characters; `problem` at most 300; `ran` at most 15 words; `item` must be one of the items assigned to this reviewer, otherwise `unknown_item`. A row that breaks a limit is kept for coverage and flagged `limits_violated`; it cannot be promoted.
6. A second line for the same item is `dup_line`; the first wins.

Earlier assistant messages in the transcript are read for the `transcript` corpus (DD-2) and for diagnosis only. They never feed promotion and never change `ledger_missing` (`MR` 3.0.4).

### 9.2 Checks (per reviewer, per row)

| # | Check | Result recorded |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every item assigned to the reviewer has a ledger line | `missing_line: [S5, ...]`. No re-ask (time). |
| 2 | `quote_plan` is a flattened substring of the candidate (`FND.locate` is non-empty) | `quote_plan_ok` |
| 3 | `quote_other` is a flattened substring of the source, the candidate, a printed tool line of this item, or a tool result of the reviewer's own transcript | `quote_other_ok`, `corpus` |
| 4 | Row support. `quotes_supported`: `quote_plan_ok` and `quote_other_ok` and the two flattened quotes differ. `search_supported`: `quote_plan_ok` and `quote_other_ok` and `corpus` is `sheet` or `transcript` | `supported = quotes_supported or search_supported` |

All substring tests use `FND.flat` and `FND.locate`, so a quote that wraps a plan line still matches (REQ-14).

### 9.3 Linking, demotion, promotion

**Link.** A findings line is linked to a ledger row when its `probe` equals the row's `item`, or when the row's flattened `quote_plan` lies inside the finding's flattened `anchor` (`MR` 3.0.5, "Linking"). A `probe` that names an item not assigned to this reviewer is `probe_unknown` and does not link.

**Demotion** (applies to linked findings only, DD-3). A linked finding with `blocking: true` is set to `blocking: false` (severity stays; a `CRITICAL` or `MAJOR` non-blocking line is valid) when any of these holds. Each cause is counted separately, because format-induced demotions must be reported (INV-007):

| Cause | Condition |
|---|---|
| `row_unsupported` | the linked row is `PROBLEM` and `supported` is false |
| `row_unsure` | the linked row is `UNSURE` |
| `no_cb3` | the finding does not carry the CB-3 sentence (below) |
| `row_missing` | the linked row failed to parse (a format error line) |

A linked finding whose row is `OK` is left alone and counted as `ok_but_finding`.

**The CB-3 sentence.** The text `An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds` (compared after flattening, case-insensitive) must appear in the finding's `claim`, or in the report text within 12 lines of a line that mentions the finding's id as a whole word, before the findings block.

**Promotion** (a `PROBLEM` row with no linked findings line; `UNSURE` and `OK` rows are never promoted). The check never writes a claim of its own:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `id` | `P` + the item id (for example `PS3`); a numeric suffix is added if the id is already used in the block |
| `severity`, `blocking` | `MINOR`, `false` |
| `category` | the class card's `promote_category` (DD-11) |
| `anchor` | the row's `quote_plan` (a row with an empty `quote_plan` is not promoted) |
| `claim` | the row's `problem`, copied unchanged |
| `refs` | `[]` |
| telemetry | `"class": "<C1-C8>"`, `"probe": "<item id>"`, `"src": "ledger"` |

The line is built as an object and validated with `_check_finding` (REQ-15) against the ids already in the block; it is inserted as the last line inside the one existing `findings-v1` block, before the closing fence; it is never written as a second block. On any failure the row is logged in `check.json: promotion_failures` and skipped. Promoted findings are counted apart from reviewer findings in every metric.

**Telemetry on reviewer lines.** For every linked line the check adds `"class"` (from the item) and keeps the reviewer's `probe`. `FND` does not reject unknown keys (`_check_finding`, lines 90-121, has no key whitelist), and `LED.merge_round` copies only fixed fields into a ledger row (`row` at lines 184-202; members carry only round, reviewer id, finding id and blocking). So the keys never reach `merged-1.md` or `merged/ledger.json`. Telemetry is therefore read from `check/<rid>.checked.md` and joined to the merged ledger through `(reviewer_id, finding id)`. REQ-11 is a test with the real merge.

**Block repair is out of scope.** If the `findings-v1` block is missing, unclosed or duplicated, the check changes nothing for that reviewer (it cannot insert a promoted line) and records `block_unusable`. The merge then handles the reviewer as it does today (`LED.merge_round` skips a reviewer with an invalid block for clearing but keeps its parsable lines).

### 9.4 Outputs

`check/<rid>.ledger.json`: the parsed rows with every check result. `check/<rid>.checked.md`: the report with demotions and promotions applied (the raw `reviews/<rid>.md` is never edited). `check/check.json`:

```
{ "ledger_missing": [rid, ...], "format_errors": n, "normalised_verdict": n, "dup_line": n, "unknown_item": n,
  "probe_unknown": n, "missing_line": {rid: [item, ...]}, "rows": {"OK": n, "PROBLEM": n, "UNSURE": n},
  "demoted": {"row_unsupported": n, "row_unsure": n, "no_cb3": n, "row_missing": n},
  "format_induced_demotions": n,   // demotions whose row failed only on a quote-match or a parse, not on content
  "promoted": n, "promotion_failures": [...], "ok_but_finding": n, "block_unusable": [rid, ...] }
```

`format_induced_demotions` counts demotions where the row's `problem` text is non-empty and both quotes are present but a quote test failed, or a line failed to parse. It is the number that tells whether the 0.914 squared figure of `MR` 3.0.5 item 4 shows up in practice.

### 9.5 Flags

| Flag | Meaning | Written to |
|---|---|---|
| `fallback=true` | the Z0 brief was run because the pre-pass or the render failed | `run.json` |
| `no_trigger=true` | the sheet was empty; the brief equals Z0's | `run.json` |
| `no_source=true` | no source file; CB-1 and E5 not applied | `run.json` |
| `check_skipped=true` | the post-run check raised; demotion and promotion skipped for the whole run and the findings block merged as written | `run.json`, `check/error.log` |
| `ledger_missing` | per reviewer, in section 9.1 | `check.json` |

import random
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

SW = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(SW))

from scaffold import clock, fnd, judge  # noqa: E402

SCHEMA = "sweep-metrics/1"
CONSISTENT_NUM, CONSISTENT_DEN = 6, 10  # reached in at least 60% of the runs
HALF_NUM, HALF_DEN = 1, 2
WILSON_Z = 1.96
DIGITS = 6
METRICS = (
    "found_fraction",
    "found_blocking_fraction",
    "share_runs_found_half",
    "run_jaccard",
    "consistent_items",
    "stable_hit_rate",
    "wrong_blockers",
    "nonprobe_findings",
    "elapsed_s",
    "output_tokens",
    "kills",
    "invalid",
    "retries",
    "fallbacks",
    "class_reach",
    "ledger_headings",
    "ok_rate_planted",
)


class AnalysisError(Exception):
    """A run folder or an argument that cannot be analysed (never swallowed: the caller sees the reason)."""


@dataclass
class Run:
    name: str
    arm: str
    doc: str
    block: object
    fallback: bool
    reason: object
    elapsed: float
    reviewers: dict  # rid -> {"status", "attempts", "tokens", "nonprobe"}
    panel: str | None = None
    slowest: float | None = None  # timing.json slowest_reviewer_s: the run's own b
    found_any: frozenset | None = None
    found_blocking: frozenset | None = None
    gt_total: int = 0
    wrong: int = 0
    path: Path | None = field(default=None, repr=False)


# --- reading ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _json(path: Path):
    try:
        return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        raise AnalysisError(f"{path}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}") from e


def _report_nonprobe(path: Path) -> int:
    """Findings lines of one report that are neither probe lines nor promoted ledger lines."""
    n = 0
    for raw in fnd.lenient_lines(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
        try:
            row = json.loads(raw)
        except ValueError:
            continue  # H2 and the reviewer check left only parseable lines for an accepted report
        if not isinstance(row, dict):
            continue
        if row.get("probe") is None and row.get("src") != "ledger":
            n += 1
    return n


def _reviewer(folder: Path, rid: str, status: str) -> dict:
    cost = folder / "reviews" / f"{rid}.cost.json"
    c = _json(cost) if cost.is_file() else {}
    nonprobe = 0
    if status == "ok":  # only an accepted reviewer has a report that the merge read
        for sub in ("normalised", "reviews"):
            rep = folder / sub / f"{rid}.md"
            if rep.is_file():
                nonprobe = _report_nonprobe(rep)
                break
    return {
        "status": status,
        "attempts": int(c.get("attempts", 1)),
        "tokens": int(c.get("total_output_tokens_all", 0)),
        "nonprobe": nonprobe,
    }


def _score(folder: Path):
    key = folder / "scoring" / "label-key.json"
    if not key.is_file():
        return None
    score = Path(_json(key)["dir"]) / "score.json"
    return _json(score) if score.is_file() else None


def load_run(folder, scores=True) -> Run:
    folder = Path(folder)
    meta = _json(folder / "run.json")
    timing = folder / "timing.json"
    if not timing.is_file():
        raise AnalysisError(f"{folder}: run.json without timing.json")
    t = _json(timing)
    status = {
        rid: v["status"] for rid, v in (meta.get("reviewer_status") or {}).items()
    }
    run = Run(
        name=folder.name,
        arm=meta["arm"],
        doc=meta["doc"],
        block=meta.get("block"),
        fallback=bool(meta.get("fallback")),
        reason=meta.get("reason"),
        elapsed=float(t["panel_elapsed_s"]),
        reviewers={rid: _reviewer(folder, rid, st) for rid, st in status.items()},
        panel=meta.get("panel"),
        slowest=t.get("slowest_reviewer_s"),
        path=folder,
    )
    if scores:
        s = _score(folder)
        if s is None:
            raise AnalysisError(f"{folder}: no judge score file")
        run.found_any = frozenset(s["gt_covered_any"])
        run.found_blocking = frozenset(s["gt_covered_blocking"])
        run.gt_total = int(s["gt_total"])
        run.wrong = int(s["wrong_blockers"])
    return run


def load_runs(stage_dir, scores=True) -> list[Run]:
    """Every run folder under stage_dir that holds a run.json, in name order."""
    root = Path(stage_dir)
    if not root.is_dir():
        raise AnalysisError(f"{root} is not a folder")
    runs = [
        load_run(f, scores)
        for f in sorted(root.iterdir())
        if (f / "run.json").is_file()
    ]
    if not runs:
        raise AnalysisError(f"no run folder under {root}")
    return runs


def load_classes(gt_path, doc) -> dict:
    """{item id: class} from a ground-truth file the caller named: a file (every document) or a folder (DIR/<doc>.json)."""
    p = Path(gt_path)
    if p.is_dir():
        p = p / f"{doc}.json"
    return {i["id"]: i["class"] for i in _json(p)["items"]}


# --- arithmetic -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _mean(xs):
    return sum(xs) / len(xs) if xs else None


def median(xs):
    s = sorted(xs)
    n = len(s)
    if not n:
        return None
    return s[n // 2] if n % 2 else (s[n // 2 - 1] + s[n // 2]) / 2


def percentile(xs, q):
    """Linear interpolation between the closest ranks (q from 0 to 1)."""
    s = sorted(xs)
    if not s:
        return None
    pos = (len(s) - 1) * q
    lo = math.floor(pos)
    hi = min(lo + 1, len(s) - 1)
    return s[lo] + (s[hi] - s[lo]) * (pos - lo)


def wilson(k, n, z=WILSON_Z):
    if n == 0:
        return None
    p = k / n
    d = 1 + z * z / n
    c = (p + z * z / (2 * n)) / d
    h = z * math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z * z / (4 * n * n)) / d
    return [max(0.0, c - h), min(1.0, c + h)]


def _r(x):
    """Round every float of a nested result (the output is stable and compares with an expected file)."""
    if isinstance(x, float):
        return round(x, DIGITS)
    if isinstance(x, dict):
        return {k: _r(v) for k, v in x.items()}
    if isinstance(x, (list, tuple)):
        return [_r(v) for v in x]
    return x


# --- the metrics (one definition each) ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _write(obj, out):
    p = _writable(out)
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p.write_text(
        json.dumps(obj, indent=1, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    return p


def cmd_metrics(a):
    runs = load_runs(a.runs)
    classes = None
    if a.gt:
        classes = {d: load_classes(a.gt, d) for d in sorted({r.doc for r in runs})}
    _write(metrics(runs, classes), a.out)


def cmd_d1(a):
    _write(d1_inputs(load_runs(a.runs, scores=False), a.arm, a.base), a.out)


def _runs_dir(a) -> Path:
    if a.runs:
        return Path(a.runs)
    if a.stage:
        # `all --stage 1` reads SW/runs/stage1; the other commands take the folder name (`audit-judges stage1`)
        return SW / "runs" / (f"stage{a.stage}" if a.cmd == "all" else a.stage)
    raise AnalysisError("give a stage name or --runs")


def judge_folders(runs_dir) -> list:
    """The judge folders that the label keys of the run folders name: the first judge and, when there is one, the second."""
    out = []
    for f in sorted(Path(runs_dir).iterdir()):
        key = f / "scoring" / "label-key.json"
        if key.is_file():
            k = _json(key)
            out.append(k["dir"])
            if k.get("second"):
                out.append(k["second"]["dir"])
    return out


def _gt_file(gt, doc) -> Path:
    p = Path(gt)
    return p / f"{doc}.json" if p.is_dir() else p


def cmd_all(a):
    runs = load_runs(_runs_dir(a))
    sets, out = load_sets(a.packages), Path(a.out)
    classes = gt_by_doc = None
    if a.gt:
        docs = sorted({r.doc for r in runs})
        classes = {d: load_classes(a.gt, d) for d in docs}
        gt_by_doc = {
            d: {
                "items": _json(_gt_file(a.gt, d))["items"],
                "text": (Path(a.cand_root) / d / "candidate.md").read_text(
                    encoding="utf-8"
                ),
            }
            for d in docs
        }
    result = gates(runs, a.arm, a.base, a.checklist, sets, classes)
    _write(metrics(runs, classes), out / "metrics.json")
    _write(result, out / "gates.json")
    _write(result["gates"]["D1"]["inputs"], out / "d1.json")
    if gt_by_doc:
        rows = [
            row
            for r in runs
            for row in stage_rows(
                r, gt_by_doc[r.doc]["items"], gt_by_doc[r.doc]["text"]
            )
        ]
        stages = _writable(out / "stages.jsonl")
        stages.write_text(
            "".join(json.dumps(x, sort_keys=True) + "\n" for x in rows),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        _write(ok_rate_planted(runs, gt_by_doc, sets), out / "ok_rate_planted.json")
    audit = judge.audit(judge_folders(_runs_dir(a)))
    _write(audit, out / "judge_audit.json")
    report = render_report(
        runs, result, shares(runs), ledger_headings(runs), label=a.label, audit=audit
    )
    _writable(out / "report.md").write_text(report, encoding="utf-8")
    print(result["outcome"]["text"])


def cmd_audit_judges(a):
    audit = judge.audit(judge_folders(_runs_dir(a)))
    _write(audit, a.out)
    print(f"judge audit: {audit['checked']} checked, {audit['bad']} bad")
    return 1 if audit["bad"] else 0


def cmd_sample_second_judge(a):
    ids = [
        f.name
        for f in sorted(_runs_dir(a).iterdir())
        if (f / "run.json").is_file() and (f / "merged" / "merged-1.md").is_file()
    ]
    for i in judge.sample(ids, a.seed):
        print(i)


def cmd_compliance(a):
    result = compliance(a.runs)
    _write(result, a.out)
    print(
        f"ledger_missing {result['ledger_missing']} of {result['reviewers_checked']}: {'go' if result['go'] else 'no go'}"
    )
    return 0 if result["go"] else 1


def cmd_prereg(a):
    owner = _json(Path(a.owner_values)) if a.owner_values else None
    record = prereg(owner)
    if a.write:
        print(_write(record, a.out))
    else:
        print(json.dumps(record, indent=1, sort_keys=True))


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="analyze.py", description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    m = sub.add_parser("metrics", help="per arm and per document metrics")
    m.add_argument("--runs", required=True)
    m.add_argument("--gt", help="a ground-truth file or folder (per-class reach)")
    m.add_argument("--out", default=str(SW / "results" / "metrics.json"))
    m.set_defaults(fn=cmd_metrics)
    d = sub.add_parser("d1", help="time inputs of gate D1")
    d.add_argument("--runs", required=True)
    d.add_argument("--arm", required=True)
    d.add_argument("--base", default="Z0")
    d.add_argument("--out", default=str(SW / "results" / "d1.json"))
    d.set_defaults(fn=cmd_d1)
    al = sub.add_parser(
        "all", help="metrics, gates D1-D7, stages.jsonl, shares and report.md"
    )
    al.add_argument(
        "--stage", help="a stage name or number: runs are read from SW/runs/stage<N>"
    )
    al.add_argument("--runs", help="the run folders (instead of SW/runs/stage<N>)")
    al.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    al.add_argument(
        "--gt", help="a ground-truth file or folder (stages, per-class reach)"
    )
    al.add_argument(
        "--cand-root",
        default=str(Path(os.environ.get("SW_SB_ROOT", "/tmp/evalsb-sweep")) / "cand"),
    )
    al.add_argument("--packages", help="a packages file (default config/packages.json)")
    al.add_argument("--arm", default="SS")
    al.add_argument("--base", default="Z0")
    al.add_argument("--checklist", default="K")
    al.add_argument("--label")
    al.set_defaults(fn=cmd_all)
    aj = sub.add_parser("audit-judges", help="audit every judge folder of a stage")
    aj.add_argument("stage", nargs="?")
    aj.add_argument("--runs")
    aj.add_argument("--out", default=str(SW / "results" / "judge_audit.json"))
    aj.set_defaults(fn=cmd_audit_judges)
    sj = sub.add_parser(
        "sample-second-judge", help="the seeded 15% sample of runs for a second judge"
    )
    sj.add_argument("stage", nargs="?")
    sj.add_argument("--runs")
    sj.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261115)
    sj.set_defaults(fn=cmd_sample_second_judge)
    co = sub.add_parser(
        "compliance",
        help="ledger_missing rate and quote validity of the compliance-spike runs",
    )
    co.add_argument("--runs", required=True)
    co.add_argument("--out", default=str(SW / "results" / "compliance.json"))
    co.set_defaults(fn=cmd_compliance)
    pr = sub.add_parser(
        "prereg",
        help="the pre-registration record (arms, run counts, gates, floor, act bands)",
    )
    pr.add_argument("--write", action="store_true")
    pr.add_argument(
        "--owner-values",
        help="a JSON file: selection_recall_floor, act_bands, ground_truth_sha256",
    )
    pr.add_argument("--out", default=str(SW / "config" / "prereg.json"))
    pr.set_defaults(fn=cmd_prereg)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        return args.fn(args) or 0
    except AnalysisError as e:
        print(f"analyze: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

===
### 11.5 Hang guard

`hang_s = 1.5 * (b + expected_overhead)` from `t0` (INV-008). `b` comes from `config/values.json` (planning stand-ins until the same-block Z0 medians exist: ember panel 100-122 s by document, haiku 220-238, sonnet 259-302; `MR` 3.1(c)); `expected_overhead` is 29 s for SS on the ember panel (the 8 + 1 + 19 + 1 of section 12), 37 s for haiku, 31 s for sonnet, 0 for the other arms. Each reviewer is run under `timeout <hang_s - (time already used)>`. A reviewer killed by it is recorded `killed` and scored zero findings.

### 11.6 Schedule and concurrency

`bin/make-schedule.py` writes `schedule.tsv` with one line per (stage, block, arm, document, replicate) in block-randomised order (one block per replicate; the shuffle uses a recorded seed). `bin/run-schedule.sh` runs it with at most 3 panels at once, so at most 9 reviewer sessions and at most 3 ember sessions, inside the limits of `SPEC` (10 sessions) and of the precedent (4 ember). `concurrent_panels_at_start` is logged per run. Arms of one block are compared with each other, never with a run from another day (REQ-29).

### 11.7 Merge

As in `SPEC` steps 2 and 3: a per-run `resolution.json` of `{reviewers: [{reviewer_id, model}]}` for the reviewers that finished, then

`superclaude review merge --ledger RUN/merged/ledger.json --doc SB/cand/<doc>/candidate.md --round 1 --report <rid>=RUN/normalised/<rid>.md ... --resolution RUN/resolution.json --out RUN/merged/merged-1.md`

A reviewer that was killed or invalid is simply absent from `--report`. If the merge refuses the round (no valid block in any report), the run is recorded `merge_refused` and scored zero; it is not re-run (intention to treat).

## 12. Time budget against the +35% rule

===
### 14.3 Files the analysis script reads and writes (`analysis/analyze.py`, REQ-39)

It reads only the run folders, the judge outputs and `config/`. It writes `results/metrics.json` and `results/report.md`.

| Output | Content |
|---|---|
| per arm, per document | found fraction per run; share of runs that find at least half the items; run-to-run Jaccard of found sets; stable-hit rate; wrong blockers per run; found-any against found-blocking; non-probe findings per run; elapsed (mean and median); tokens; kills, retries, fallbacks, `invalid`; per-class reach with Wilson intervals |
| consistency | items reached in at least 60% of runs (3 of 5), per arm |
| gates | D1 to D7 and G0, pass or fail with the numbers; the bootstrap resamples documents first, then runs |
| shares | H share (Z0 minus Z0-raw), prompting share (K minus Z0), redesign share (SS minus Z0); never added in a headline (REQ-40) |
| `stages.jsonl` | one row per (run, ground-truth item): extraction, selection, act, merge survival, judge credit (REQ-41); `act` is a `PROBLEM` row with both quotes that links to the item (it is not conditional on selection, and the act-band measure of 15.1a is a different quantity); `merge survival` is read from `merged/ledger.json` members through `(reviewer_id, finding id)` |
| `ok_rate_planted.json` | share of `OK` verdicts on planted items (the rubber-stamp measure) |
| `judge_audit.json` | for every judge output: parseable, no API error text, `score.json` row counts equal the merged report's rows, `score.json` not older than the judge's final message (the defect `CR` line 147 describes); a second judge on a seeded 15% sample |

### 11.5 Hang guard

`hang_s = 1.5 * (b + expected_overhead)` from `t0` (INV-008). `b` comes from `config/values.json` (planning stand-ins until the same-block Z0 medians exist: ember panel 100-122 s by document, haiku 220-238, sonnet 259-302; `MR` 3.1(c)); `expected_overhead` is 29 s for SS on the ember panel (the 8 + 1 + 19 + 1 of section 12), 37 s for haiku, 31 s for sonnet, 0 for the other arms. Each reviewer is run under `timeout <hang_s - (time already used)>`. A reviewer killed by it is recorded `killed` and scored zero findings.

### 11.6 Schedule and concurrency

`bin/make-schedule.py` writes `schedule.tsv` with one line per (stage, block, arm, document, replicate) in block-randomised order (one block per replicate; the shuffle uses a recorded seed). `bin/run-schedule.sh` runs it with at most 3 panels at once, so at most 9 reviewer sessions and at most 3 ember sessions, inside the limits of `SPEC` (10 sessions) and of the precedent (4 ember). `concurrent_panels_at_start` is logged per run. Arms of one block are compared with each other, never with a run from another day (REQ-29).

### 11.7 Merge

As in `SPEC` steps 2 and 3: a per-run `resolution.json` of `{reviewers: [{reviewer_id, model}]}` for the reviewers that finished, then

`superclaude review merge --ledger RUN/merged/ledger.json --doc SB/cand/<doc>/candidate.md --round 1 --report <rid>=RUN/normalised/<rid>.md ... --resolution RUN/resolution.json --out RUN/merged/merged-1.md`

A reviewer that was killed or invalid is simply absent from `--report`. If the merge refuses the round (no valid block in any report), the run is recorded `merge_refused` and scored zero; it is not re-run (intention to treat).

## 12. Time budget against the +35% rule

===
### 14.3 Files the analysis script reads and writes (`analysis/analyze.py`, REQ-39)

It reads only the run folders, the judge outputs and `config/`. It writes `results/metrics.json` and `results/report.md`.

| Output | Content |
|---|---|
| per arm, per document | found fraction per run; share of runs that find at least half the items; run-to-run Jaccard of found sets; stable-hit rate; wrong blockers per run; found-any against found-blocking; non-probe findings per run; elapsed (mean and median); tokens; kills, retries, fallbacks, `invalid`; per-class reach with Wilson intervals |
| consistency | items reached in at least 60% of runs (3 of 5), per arm |
| gates | D1 to D7 and G0, pass or fail with the numbers; the bootstrap resamples documents first, then runs |
| shares | H share (Z0 minus Z0-raw), prompting share (K minus Z0), redesign share (SS minus Z0); never added in a headline (REQ-40) |
| `stages.jsonl` | one row per (run, ground-truth item): extraction, selection, act, merge survival, judge credit (REQ-41); `act` is a `PROBLEM` row with both quotes that links to the item (it is not conditional on selection, and the act-band measure of 15.1a is a different quantity); `merge survival` is read from `merged/ledger.json` members through `(reviewer_id, finding id)` |
| `ok_rate_planted.json` | share of `OK` verdicts on planted items (the rubber-stamp measure) |
| `judge_audit.json` | for every judge output: parseable, no API error text, `score.json` row counts equal the merged report's rows, `score.json` not older than the judge's final message (the defect `CR` line 147 describes); a second judge on a seeded 15% sample |

253	
254	Counts. `MR` 5.4 gives Stage 1 as 95 panel runs: 80 for the four arms Z0, K, SS and RL on four documents with 5 runs each, and 15 for Z0-raw on three documents. This design builds no RL arm, so the Stage 1 schedule above has 3 arms x 4 documents x 5 = 60 runs plus 15 Z0-raw = **75 panel runs** (225 reviewer runs). The 20 RL runs of `MR` are not part of this schedule.
255	
256	### E. Models: Stage 2 (only for an arm that passes D1, D2 or D3 on Stage 1)
257	
258	```
259	E1  planted set (6 plans, Z0 and SS, 3 runs):      $PYRUN $SW/bin/make-schedule.py --stage 2 --set planted --arms z0,ss --reps 3 ...      36 runs
260	E2  clean twins (6 plans, 2 runs):                 ... --set twins --arms z0,ss --reps 2 ...                                               24 runs
261	E3  spec HO-5 (5 runs):                            ... --set spec --arms z0,ss --reps 5 ...                                                10 runs
262	E4  documentation arm (8 documents, 3 runs):       ... --set docs --arms z0,ss --reps 3 ...                                                48 runs
263	E5  haiku panel (4 documents, 3 runs):             ... --set holdout4 --panel haiku --arms z0,ss --reps 3 ...                              24 runs
264	E6  sonnet panel (3 documents, 2 runs):            ... --set holdout3 --panel sonnet --arms z0,ss --reps 2 ...                             12 runs
265	E7  then, as in D3 to D6 with --stage 2
266	```
267	
268	Stage 2 without RL is 36 + 24 + 10 + 48 + 24 + 12 = **154 panel runs** (`MR` gives 231 with RL). With Stage 1 the total is 75 + 154 = **229 panel runs**, about 687 reviewer runs (`MR`: 326 panel runs, about 978 reviewer runs, with both redesigns).
269	
270	### F. Derivation-set check (reported, never used for a decision)
271	
272	```
273	F1  run Z0 and SS once on the three study packages (derivation set):  $PYRUN $SW/bin/make-schedule.py --stage d --set derivation --arms z0,ss --reps 1 ...
274	F2  $PYRUN $SW/analysis/analyze.py all --stage d --out $SW/results/derivation --label derivation-only
275	```
276	
277	### G. Decision
278	
279	`analysis/analyze.py all` prints the outcome row of `MR` 5.8 for SS against Z0 and K: neither redesign passes means keep Z0; SS passing alone adopts SS; "SS beats K by at least 0.04" is gate D7. Adoption then follows `IMPLEMENTATION.md` step 16.
280	
281	## 6. Definition of done for the implementation
282	
283	The implementation is done when all of the following hold, each shown by an output, not by a statement:
284	
285	1. `$T $SW/tests -q -m "not slow and not freeze"` exits 0 and its summary line is saved to `SW/results/tests-final.log`.
286	2. `uv run --frozen --project $REPO ruff check $SW` and `ruff format --check $SW` exit 0.
287	3. `uv run --frozen --project $REPO pytest -p no:cacheprovider $REPO/tests/review -q` still exits 0.
288	4. Every row of section 3 is either backed by a passing test or by an M record that exists on disk; the list of M records still open is printed by `bin/open-manual-checks.sh`.
289	5. `git status` shows no change under `src/`, `tests/`, `.claude/` or `.dev/tasks/` made by the implementation.
290	6. The freeze (`IMPLEMENTATION.md` step 14) has not been done before items 1 to 5 hold, and the freeze tests (`-m freeze`) pass.
291	
292	What "done" does not mean: that SS works. Whether the sheet raises the found fraction is decided only by Stage 1 and Stage 2 (section 5), and the power of that experiment is low (`MR` 5.9): a pass is evidence, not proof.
